title: Horizon scanning and foresight in future enabling digital technologies (CSA)
destinationDetails:
Leadership in frontier technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Quantum, Photonics and Semiconductors is essential to Europe’s economic security and global competitiveness. Building on the ambition of becoming the “AI Continent” and in line with the concrete actions devised in the Apply AI Strategy[1], the EU will consolidate its world-class research ecosystem through initiatives like the RAISE network of AI science labs, the development of safe and efficient frontier AI models, and the deployment of next-generation AI agents and robotics in strategic sectors. In parallel, a long-term quantum strategy will reinforce Europe’s excellence across quantum computing, sensing and communication, supported by new infrastructures and standardisation to secure technological sovereignty. Photonics and semiconductor technologies will remain critical enablers for the digital and green transitions, with investments in advanced integrated photonic devices and resilient semiconductor ecosystems ensuring Europe’s capacity to innovate, scale and compete globally. Foresight and support to emerging materials and technologies will further strengthen Europe’s position at the cutting edge to make sure Europe’s does not miss the emergence of new disruptive technologies, aligning with the Draghi report and the Competitiveness Compass to secure a cohesive, sovereign and future-proof European industrial base.

Legal entities established in China are not eligible to participate in both Research and Innovation Actions (RIAs) and Innovation Actions (IAs) falling under this destination. For additional information please see “Restrictions on the participation of legal entities established in China” found in General Annex B of the General Annexes.

[1] COM(2025)723 Apply AI Strategy
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

  • European leadership in foresight activities on future enabling technologies and their transformational potential in industrial, societal and environmental terms.
  • Increased collaboration between academia, industry players and other relevant stakeholders in iterative and multidisciplinary approaches for co-creating the enabling technologies of the future.
  • Alignment with national or regional initiatives creating an expanding innovation ecosystem, anchored in local contexts across Europe, for selected emerging technologies.
  • Accelerating the pick-up of novel advanced technology by industry and society.

Scope:

Proposals should establish a forum for emerging interdisciplinary areas and new technological visions.

Proposals should enable and support a broad range of participants (across disciplines in science and engineering, RTOs, industry sectors, stakeholders) to meet, mutually inspire, cooperate and develop together innovative ideas for future enabling digital technologies covering from fundamental research up to proof of concept.

Proposals should involve and be driven by representatives of the relevant actors of the field (e.g., academia, RTOs, industry including SMEs).

Proposals should consider civil society engagement for seeking wider input.

Proposals should connect with analogous EC-internal activities, either ongoing (e.g. FOSI4EIC involving EISMEA and JRC) or foreseen, such as the Competitiveness Coordination Tool and the technology observatory envisaged in the FP10 regulation.

Beneficiaries that intend to transfer ownership or grant an exclusive licence must formally notify the granting authority (i.e. DG-CNECT and HaDEA) before the intended transfer or licensing takes place and the granting authority may up to four years after the end of the action object to a transfer of ownership or the exclusive licensing of results.

destinationDetails:
Through the European Partnership on Virtual Worlds, Europe will drive investment in advanced hardware, immersive interaction, and seamless integration across the Telco-Cloud-to-Edge continuum, enabling lifelike multisensory experiences and fully interoperable platforms. These efforts will enhance Europe’s capacity to innovate, deploy, and scale trustworthy virtual worlds, thereby strengthening competitiveness, resilience, and alignment with EU values.At the same time, a robust Web 4.0 architectural framework — underpinned by open-source solutions and shared standards — will be essential to ensure interoperability, decentralisation, and trust. By deepening Europe’s engagement in international digital standardisation, the Union will help shape global norms in line with its strategic interests, technological sovereignty, and core values.

descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

Proposals are expected to contribute to the following outcomes:

  • Increasing the participation and influence of European experts in digital standardisation to promote EU values and strategic interests, contributing to strengthen EU competitiveness in the digital field.
  • Improvement of the skills of European experts, especially from SMEs, R&I institutions, Open-Source community, academia and societal stakeholders, to successfully contribute and lead in the development of digital standards.
  • Development and update of standardisation landscapes and gap analyses of key digital technologies as outlined in the Rolling Plan for ICT Standardisation.
  • Provision of foresight analyses regarding standardisation in new emerging technologies to identify short and medium-term digital standardisation needs to support EU policies and anticipate appropriate participation by EU stakeholders.
  • More awareness of the benefits and competitive advantages of standardisation, in particular for SMEs and researchers, and more visibility of the European digital standardisation ecosystem.

Scope:

Contribute to the implementation of the EU Standardisation Strategy and other policy initiatives such as Europe’s Digital Decade, Apply AI Strategy or the Competitiveness Compass, with an emphasis on supporting the EU’s leading position in global standards-setting of key digital technologies.

The goals are inter alia to 1) strengthen the EU competitiveness in the digital domain; 2) contribute to EU tech sovereignty and 3) promote EU values and interests internationally, by empowering and financially supporting the active participation of European stakeholders in the development of digital international standards.

The objective is to reinforce the presence of experts from the EU and associated Horizon Europe countries in global digital standards setting, especially those coming from SMEs, R&I institutions, Open-Source community, academia and societal stakeholders.

To achieve this objective, proposals under this topic should provide for:

  • Setting up of a management facility to support contributions and leadership (e.g. chairing of technical committees, convenor positions) of European specialists in activities in relation to global digital standardisation
  • When relevant, support financially the hosting of international standardisation meetings (e.g. 3GPP, ISO/IEC JTC1) and workshops in Europe to ease the participation of European experts
  • Landscape and gap analysis of standardisation activities in key digital priority areas, as outlined in the Annual Union Work Programme and the Rolling Plan for ICT standardisation, including identification of new emerging technology areas.
  • Promotion of the relevance and benefits of digital standardisation, especially for strengthening the competitiveness of EU industry, driving sustainability, achieving tech sovereignty, and promoting EU values. The proposal shall build synergies with other similar EU- and national-funded initiatives. It shall also include actions, including development of tools and materials, to promote education and skills on standardisation.

Beneficiaries that intend to transfer ownership or grant an exclusive licence must formally notify the granting authority (i.e. DG-CNECT and HaDEA) before the intended transfer or licensing takes place and the granting authority may up to four years after the end of the action object to a transfer of ownership or the exclusive licensing of results.

The proposal should take into account the previous activities carried out at least in terms of educational material and facilities for funding experts within the topics ICT-40-2017 (implemented by the StandICT.eu project), ICT-45-2020 (implemented under StandICT.eu2023 project), HORIZON-CL4-2022-RESILIENCE-01-21 (implemented under StandICT.eu 2026) and HORIZON-CL4-2024-HUMAN-03-04 (implemented under StandICT.eu 2029).

See website: http://www.standict.eu.

title: Horizon scanning and foresight in future enabling digital technologies (CSA)
destinationDetails:
Leadership in frontier technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Quantum, Photonics and Semiconductors is essential to Europe’s economic security and global competitiveness. Building on the ambition of becoming the “AI Continent” and in line with the concrete actions devised in the Apply AI Strategy[1], the EU will consolidate its world-class research ecosystem through initiatives like the RAISE network of AI science labs, the development of safe and efficient frontier AI models, and the deployment of next-generation AI agents and robotics in strategic sectors. In parallel, a long-term quantum strategy will reinforce Europe’s excellence across quantum computing, sensing and communication, supported by new infrastructures and standardisation to secure technological sovereignty. Photonics and semiconductor technologies will remain critical enablers for the digital and green transitions, with investments in advanced integrated photonic devices and resilient semiconductor ecosystems ensuring Europe’s capacity to innovate, scale and compete globally. Foresight and support to emerging materials and technologies will further strengthen Europe’s position at the cutting edge to make sure Europe’s does not miss the emergence of new disruptive technologies, aligning with the Draghi report and the Competitiveness Compass to secure a cohesive, sovereign and future-proof European industrial base.

Legal entities established in China are not eligible to participate in both Research and Innovation Actions (RIAs) and Innovation Actions (IAs) falling under this destination. For additional information please see “Restrictions on the participation of legal entities established in China” found in General Annex B of the General Annexes.

[1] COM(2025)723 Apply AI Strategy
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

  • European leadership in foresight activities on future enabling technologies and their transformational potential in industrial, societal and environmental terms.
  • Increased collaboration between academia, industry players and other relevant stakeholders in iterative and multidisciplinary approaches for co-creating the enabling technologies of the future.
  • Alignment with national or regional initiatives creating an expanding innovation ecosystem, anchored in local contexts across Europe, for selected emerging technologies.
  • Accelerating the pick-up of novel advanced technology by industry and society.

Scope:

Proposals should establish a forum for emerging interdisciplinary areas and new technological visions.

Proposals should enable and support a broad range of participants (across disciplines in science and engineering, RTOs, industry sectors, stakeholders) to meet, mutually inspire, cooperate and develop together innovative ideas for future enabling digital technologies covering from fundamental research up to proof of concept.

Proposals should involve and be driven by representatives of the relevant actors of the field (e.g., academia, RTOs, industry including SMEs).

Proposals should consider civil society engagement for seeking wider input.

Proposals should connect with analogous EC-internal activities, either ongoing (e.g. FOSI4EIC involving EISMEA and JRC) or foreseen, such as the Competitiveness Coordination Tool and the technology observatory envisaged in the FP10 regulation.

Beneficiaries that intend to transfer ownership or grant an exclusive licence must formally notify the granting authority (i.e. DG-CNECT and HaDEA) before the intended transfer or licensing takes place and the granting authority may up to four years after the end of the action object to a transfer of ownership or the exclusive licensing of results.

title: Secure PQC implementations, Cryptanalysis and Post-quantum Digital Trust
callTitle: Indirectly Managed Action by the ECCC (2027)
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

Proposals are expected to contribute one or more of the following:

  • Practical robust implementations of PQC schemes that can withstand implementation attacks including side-channel attacks, fault attacks and combined attacks, and design of automated tools for evaluating the security of PQC implementations. Comprehensive guidelines for implementing countermeasures against a wide range of attacks;
  • Advances in understanding the quantum hardness of mathematical problem classes; new quantum algorithms and improvements in quantum programming and implementation; security validation methods; design of post-quantum schemes with improved security against quantum and AI-based attacks;
  • Post-quantum schemes and protocols to support privacy-friendly applications and services, ncluding the secure and private use of electronic identities. Design of new digital signatures, key encapsulation mechanisms, and other schemes or use of existing ones to build new verification protocols.

Scope:

Securing PQC algorithm implementations is vital to protect against implementation attacks, such as side channel attacks, fault attacks and combinations of these, which may be amplified by deep learning. Current countermeasures incur significant overhead, and new approaches are needed to balance security and performance. Formal verification tools and methodologies can help achieve this goal and provide machine-readable evidence. Furthermore, to boost confidence in PQC systems, their security should be assessed, including the potential impact of new quantum algorithms or new optimizations of existing ones, also combined with AI.

Another key research area is digital trust in the post-quantum era, which requires transforming various areas, such as secure identities, data protection, access to essential services, and applications such as backup recovery, browser extensions and others into trusted and reliable solutions, via new post-quantum schemes and advanced building blocks for privacy-enhancing protocols.

Proposals should address one of the following technology areas:

  • Development of solutions to prevent implementation attacks, balancing security, performance and cost; research in new attacks, including AI-powered ones, and/or combination of attacks, to inform secure design; creation of testing frameworks for automated security evaluations; improvement of formal verification methodologies.
  • Quantum hardness analysis, via the study of the impact of new quantum algorithms or improvement of existing quantum algorithm implementations as well as the impact of AI-supported quantum attacks; analysis of cryptanalysis results; design of new post-quantum schemes using the information of the advances achieved/ fine-tuning of parameters sets.
  • Design of quantum-resistant schemes and protocols supporting the field of privacy-friendly applications and services, including electronic identities, verification protocols and pseudonymous access options, protocols for attestation and anonymous attestation, for real world scenarios, via the design of new digital signature schemes and key encapsulation mechanisms, design of advanced cryptographic schemes, and usage of existing schemes in new protocols, for post-quantum digital identity and digital trust systems.

title: Secure PQC implementations, Cryptanalysis and Post-quantum Digital Trust
callTitle: Indirectly Managed Action by the ECCC (2027)
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

Proposals are expected to contribute one or more of the following:

  • Practical robust implementations of PQC schemes that can withstand implementation attacks including side-channel attacks, fault attacks and combined attacks, and design of automated tools for evaluating the security of PQC implementations. Comprehensive guidelines for implementing countermeasures against a wide range of attacks;
  • Advances in understanding the quantum hardness of mathematical problem classes; new quantum algorithms and improvements in quantum programming and implementation; security validation methods; design of post-quantum schemes with improved security against quantum and AI-based attacks;
  • Post-quantum schemes and protocols to support privacy-friendly applications and services, ncluding the secure and private use of electronic identities. Design of new digital signatures, key encapsulation mechanisms, and other schemes or use of existing ones to build new verification protocols.

Scope:

Securing PQC algorithm implementations is vital to protect against implementation attacks, such as side channel attacks, fault attacks and combinations of these, which may be amplified by deep learning. Current countermeasures incur significant overhead, and new approaches are needed to balance security and performance. Formal verification tools and methodologies can help achieve this goal and provide machine-readable evidence. Furthermore, to boost confidence in PQC systems, their security should be assessed, including the potential impact of new quantum algorithms or new optimizations of existing ones, also combined with AI.

Another key research area is digital trust in the post-quantum era, which requires transforming various areas, such as secure identities, data protection, access to essential services, and applications such as backup recovery, browser extensions and others into trusted and reliable solutions, via new post-quantum schemes and advanced building blocks for privacy-enhancing protocols.

Proposals should address one of the following technology areas:

  • Development of solutions to prevent implementation attacks, balancing security, performance and cost; research in new attacks, including AI-powered ones, and/or combination of attacks, to inform secure design; creation of testing frameworks for automated security evaluations; improvement of formal verification methodologies.
  • Quantum hardness analysis, via the study of the impact of new quantum algorithms or improvement of existing quantum algorithm implementations as well as the impact of AI-supported quantum attacks; analysis of cryptanalysis results; design of new post-quantum schemes using the information of the advances achieved/ fine-tuning of parameters sets.
  • Design of quantum-resistant schemes and protocols supporting the field of privacy-friendly applications and services, including electronic identities, verification protocols and pseudonymous access options, protocols for attestation and anonymous attestation, for real world scenarios, via the design of new digital signature schemes and key encapsulation mechanisms, design of advanced cryptographic schemes, and usage of existing schemes in new protocols, for post-quantum digital identity and digital trust systems.

title: Facilitate the engagement of European stakeholders in international digital standardisation (CSA)
destinationDetails:
Through the European Partnership on Virtual Worlds, Europe will drive investment in advanced hardware, immersive interaction, and seamless integration across the Telco-Cloud-to-Edge continuum, enabling lifelike multisensory experiences and fully interoperable platforms. These efforts will enhance Europe’s capacity to innovate, deploy, and scale trustworthy virtual worlds, thereby strengthening competitiveness, resilience, and alignment with EU values.At the same time, a robust Web 4.0 architectural framework — underpinned by open-source solutions and shared standards — will be essential to ensure interoperability, decentralisation, and trust. By deepening Europe’s engagement in international digital standardisation, the Union will help shape global norms in line with its strategic interests, technological sovereignty, and core values.

Legal entities established in China are not eligible to participate in both Research and Innovation Actions (RIAs) and Innovation Actions (IAs) falling under this destination. For additional information please see “Restrictions on the participation of legal entities established in China” found in General Annex B of the General Annexes.
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

Proposals are expected to contribute to the following outcomes:

  • Increasing the participation and influence of European experts in digital standardisation to promote EU values and strategic interests, contributing to strengthen EU competitiveness in the digital field.
  • Improvement of the skills of European experts, especially from SMEs, R&I institutions, Open-Source community, academia and societal stakeholders, to successfully contribute and lead in the development of digital standards.
  • Development and update of standardisation landscapes and gap analyses of key digital technologies as outlined in the Rolling Plan for ICT Standardisation.
  • Provision of foresight analyses regarding standardisation in new emerging technologies to identify short and medium-term digital standardisation needs to support EU policies and anticipate appropriate participation by EU stakeholders.
  • More awareness of the benefits and competitive advantages of standardisation, in particular for SMEs and researchers, and more visibility of the European digital standardisation ecosystem.

Scope:

Contribute to the implementation of the EU Standardisation Strategy and other policy initiatives such as Europe’s Digital Decade, Apply AI Strategy or the Competitiveness Compass, with an emphasis on supporting the EU’s leading position in global standards-setting of key digital technologies.

The goals are inter alia to 1) strengthen the EU competitiveness in the digital domain; 2) contribute to EU tech sovereignty and 3) promote EU values and interests internationally, by empowering and financially supporting the active participation of European stakeholders in the development of digital international standards.

The objective is to reinforce the presence of experts from the EU and associated Horizon Europe countries in global digital standards setting, especially those coming from SMEs, R&I institutions, Open-Source community, academia and societal stakeholders.

To achieve this objective, proposals under this topic should provide for:

  • Setting up of a management facility to support contributions and leadership (e.g. chairing of technical committees, convenor positions) of European specialists in activities in relation to global digital standardisation
  • When relevant, support financially the hosting of international standardisation meetings (e.g. 3GPP, ISO/IEC JTC1) and workshops in Europe to ease the participation of European experts
  • Landscape and gap analysis of standardisation activities in key digital priority areas, as outlined in the Annual Union Work Programme and the Rolling Plan for ICT standardisation, including identification of new emerging technology areas.
  • Promotion of the relevance and benefits of digital standardisation, especially for strengthening the competitiveness of EU industry, driving sustainability, achieving tech sovereignty, and promoting EU values. The proposal shall build synergies with other similar EU- and national-funded initiatives. It shall also include actions, including development of tools and materials, to promote education and skills on standardisation.

Beneficiaries that intend to transfer ownership or grant an exclusive licence must formally notify the granting authority (i.e. DG-CNECT and HaDEA) before the intended transfer or licensing takes place and the granting authority may up to four years after the end of the action object to a transfer of ownership or the exclusive licensing of results.

The proposal should take into account the previous activities carried out at least in terms of educational material and facilities for funding experts within the topics ICT-40-2017 (implemented by the StandICT.eu project), ICT-45-2020 (implemented under StandICT.eu2023 project), HORIZON-CL4-2022-RESILIENCE-01-21 (implemented under StandICT.eu 2026) and HORIZON-CL4-2024-HUMAN-03-04 (implemented under StandICT.eu 2029).

See website: http://www.standict.eu.

  • Promotion of the relevance and benefits of digital standardisation, especially for strengthening the competitiveness of EU industry, driving sustainability, achieving tech sovereignty, and promoting EU values. The proposal shall build synergies with other similar EU- and national-funded initiatives. It shall also include actions, including development of tools and materials, to promote education and skills on standardisation.

Beneficiaries that intend to transfer ownership or grant an exclusive licence must formally notify the granting authority (i.e. DG-CNECT and HaDEA) before the intended transfer or licensing takes place and the granting authority may up to four years after the end of the action object to a transfer of ownership or the exclusive licensing of results.

title: Secure PQC implementations, Cryptanalysis and Post-quantum Digital Trust
callTitle: Indirectly Managed Action by the ECCC (2027)
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

Proposals are expected to contribute one or more of the following:

  • Practical robust implementations of PQC schemes that can withstand implementation attacks including side-channel attacks, fault attacks and combined attacks, and design of automated tools for evaluating the security of PQC implementations. Comprehensive guidelines for implementing countermeasures against a wide range of attacks;
  • Advances in understanding the quantum hardness of mathematical problem classes; new quantum algorithms and improvements in quantum programming and implementation; security validation methods; design of post-quantum schemes with improved security against quantum and AI-based attacks;
  • Post-quantum schemes and protocols to support privacy-friendly applications and services, ncluding the secure and private use of electronic identities. Design of new digital signatures, key encapsulation mechanisms, and other schemes or use of existing ones to build new verification protocols.

Scope:

Securing PQC algorithm implementations is vital to protect against implementation attacks, such as side channel attacks, fault attacks and combinations of these, which may be amplified by deep learning. Current countermeasures incur significant overhead, and new approaches are needed to balance security and performance. Formal verification tools and methodologies can help achieve this goal and provide machine-readable evidence. Furthermore, to boost confidence in PQC systems, their security should be assessed, including the potential impact of new quantum algorithms or new optimizations of existing ones, also combined with AI.

Another key research area is digital trust in the post-quantum era, which requires transforming various areas, such as secure identities, data protection, access to essential services, and applications such as backup recovery, browser extensions and others into trusted and reliable solutions, via new post-quantum schemes and advanced building blocks for privacy-enhancing protocols.

Proposals should address one of the following technology areas:

  • Development of solutions to prevent implementation attacks, balancing security, performance and cost; research in new attacks, including AI-powered ones, and/or combination of attacks, to inform secure design; creation of testing frameworks for automated security evaluations; improvement of formal verification methodologies.
  • Quantum hardness analysis, via the study of the impact of new quantum algorithms or improvement of existing quantum algorithm implementations as well as the impact of AI-supported quantum attacks; analysis of cryptanalysis results; design of new post-quantum schemes using the information of the advances achieved/ fine-tuning of parameters sets.
  • Design of quantum-resistant schemes and protocols supporting the field of privacy-friendly applications and services, including electronic identities, verification protocols and pseudonymous access options, protocols for attestation and anonymous attestation, for real world scenarios, via the design of new digital signature schemes and key encapsulation mechanisms, design of advanced cryptographic schemes, and usage of existing schemes in new protocols, for post-quantum digital identity and digital trust systems.

destinationDetails:
Through the European Partnership on Virtual Worlds, Europe will drive investment in advanced hardware, immersive interaction, and seamless integration across the Telco-Cloud-to-Edge continuum, enabling lifelike multisensory experiences and fully interoperable platforms. These efforts will enhance Europe’s capacity to innovate, deploy, and scale trustworthy virtual worlds, thereby strengthening competitiveness, resilience, and alignment with EU values.At the same time, a robust Web 4.0 architectural framework — underpinned by open-source solutions and shared standards — will be essential to ensure interoperability, decentralisation, and trust. By deepening Europe’s engagement in international digital standardisation, the Union will help shape global norms in line with its strategic interests, technological sovereignty, and core values.

Legal entities established in China are not eligible to participate in both Research and Innovation Actions (RIAs) and Innovation Actions (IAs) falling under this destination. For additional information please see “Restrictions on the participation of legal entities established in China” found in General Annex B of the General Annexes.
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

Proposals are expected to contribute to the following outcomes:

  • Increasing the participation and influence of European experts in digital standardisation to promote EU values and strategic interests, contributing to strengthen EU competitiveness in the digital field.
  • Improvement of the skills of European experts, especially from SMEs, R&I institutions, Open-Source community, academia and societal stakeholders, to successfully contribute and lead in the development of digital standards.
  • Development and update of standardisation landscapes and gap analyses of key digital technologies as outlined in the Rolling Plan for ICT Standardisation.
  • Provision of foresight analyses regarding standardisation in new emerging technologies to identify short and medium-term digital standardisation needs to support EU policies and anticipate appropriate participation by EU stakeholders.
  • More awareness of the benefits and competitive advantages of standardisation, in particular for SMEs and researchers, and more visibility of the European digital standardisation ecosystem.

Scope:

Contribute to the implementation of the EU Standardisation Strategy and other policy initiatives such as Europe’s Digital Decade, Apply AI Strategy or the Competitiveness Compass, with an emphasis on supporting the EU’s leading position in global standards-setting of key digital technologies.

The goals are inter alia to 1) strengthen the EU competitiveness in the digital domain; 2) contribute to EU tech sovereignty and 3) promote EU values and interests internationally, by empowering and financially supporting the active participation of European stakeholders in the development of digital international standards.

The objective is to reinforce the presence of experts from the EU and associated Horizon Europe countries in global digital standards setting, especially those coming from SMEs, R&I institutions, Open-Source community, academia and societal stakeholders.

To achieve this objective, proposals under this topic should provide for:

  • Setting up of a management facility to support contributions and leadership (e.g. chairing of technical committees, convenor positions) of European specialists in activities in relation to global digital standardisation
  • When relevant, support financially the hosting of international standardisation meetings (e.g. 3GPP, ISO/IEC JTC1) and workshops in Europe to ease the participation of European experts
  • Landscape and gap analysis of standardisation activities in key digital priority areas, as outlined in the Annual Union Work Programme and the Rolling Plan for ICT standardisation, including identification of new emerging technology areas.
  • Promotion of the relevance and benefits of digital standardisation, especially for strengthening the competitiveness of EU industry, driving sustainability, achieving tech sovereignty, and promoting EU values. The proposal shall build synergies with other similar EU- and national-funded initiatives. It shall also include actions, including development of tools and materials, to promote education and skills on standardisation.

Beneficiaries that intend to transfer ownership or grant an exclusive licence must formally notify the granting authority (i.e. DG-CNECT and HaDEA) before the intended transfer or licensing takes place and the granting authority may up to four years after the end of the action object to a transfer of ownership or the exclusive licensing of results.

The proposal should take into account the previous activities carried out at least in terms of educational material and facilities for funding experts within the topics ICT-40-2017 (implemented by the StandICT.eu project), ICT-45-2020 (implemented under StandICT.eu2023 project), HORIZON-CL4-2022-RESILIENCE-01-21 (implemented under StandICT.eu 2026) and HORIZON-CL4-2024-HUMAN-03-04 (implemented under StandICT.eu 2029).

descrito no anexo B dos anexos gerais do programa de trabalho.

Alguns países terceiros/não associados que não são automaticamente elegíveis para financiamento adotaram disposições específicas para disponibilizar financiamento aos seus participantes em projetos do Horizonte Europa. Ver as informações no Guia do Programa Horizonte Europa.

Se os projetos utilizarem dados e serviços de observação da Terra, posicionamento, navegação e/ou cronometria conexos baseados em satélites, os beneficiários devem utilizar o Copernicus e/ou o Galileo/EGNOS (podem também ser utilizados outros dados e serviços).

As organizações internacionais com sede num Estado-Membro ou país associado/país terceiro não associado são excecionalmente elegíveis para financiamento, uma vez que várias instituições internacionais estão ativas na gestão de bacias marítimas regionais e podem contribuir para as DTO regionais com os seus próprios ativos e ser os utilizadores finais.

descrito no anexo B dos anexos gerais do programa de trabalho.

4. Capacidade financeira e operacional e exclusão

5-A. Avaliação e atribuição: Critérios de adjudicação, pontuação e limiares

A fim de assegurar uma carteira equilibrada que abranja as quatro bacias diferentes da Missão[[Para efeitos da Missão Oceanos e águas, considera-se que os Estados-Membros/países associados fazem parte de uma determinada bacia marítima/fluvial se tiverem uma costa/banco fluvial no mar/rio em causa ou se contiverem bacias hidrográficas que desaguam no mar em causa]] (1. Bacia marítima do Atlântico e do Ártico, 2. Bacia do Mar Mediterrâneo, 3. Bacia do mar Báltico e do mar do Norte, 4. bacia do rio Danúbio, incluindo o mar Negro), serão concedidas subvenções às candidaturas não só por ordem de classificação, mas também, pelo menos, a uma proposta com a classificação mais elevada em cada bacia marítima, desde que as candidaturas atinjam todos os limiares.

estão descritos no Anexo D dos Anexos Gerais do Programa de Trabalho.

estão descritos no anexo F dos anexos gerais do programa de trabalho e no manual em linha.

descrito no Anexo F dos Anexos Gerais do Programa de Trabalho.

6. Estrutura jurídica e financeira das subvenções

Os beneficiários estarão sujeitos às seguintes obrigações adicionais em matéria de práticas de ciência aberta: se os projetos recolherem dados in situ e observação marinha, os beneficiários devem disponibilizá-los abertamente através da Rede Europeia de Observação e de Dados do Meio Marinho (EMODnet), com base nos princípios FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable).

callTitle: Apoio à execução da Missão Restaurar os Oceanos e as Águas
descriptionByte:
Resultado esperado:

Espera-se que os resultados do projeto contribuam para todos os seguintes resultados esperados:

  • São disponibilizados recursos regionais e locais adicionais (dados, modelos, gémeos digitais) na infraestrutura principal da DTO, o EDITO;
  • Novas aplicações digitais geminadas, colocando a tónica nas condições regionais e locais e abordando considerações regionais, incluindo as necessidades das partes interessadas, a disponibilidade de dados, etc.;
  • Reforço das capacidades regionais da gémea digital, criando na infraestrutura principal da ORDUE, o EDITO, as condições para apoiar diretamente a execução de políticas, incluindo a política para o meio marinho, e aplicações da economia azul que se baseiem nas características regionais da bacia marítima;
  • Desenvolvimento de bibliotecas regionais de cenários «e se» (what-if-scenarios), incluindo limiares de confiança e análises conexas, quantificando as condições necessárias para aumentar os níveis de confiança, etc.;
  • Apoio à monitorização e gestão sustentável dos mares regionais com novos serviços personalizados para os mares regionais.

Âmbito de aplicação:

As propostas devem estabelecer componentes regionais no âmbito da infraestrutura principal do EDITO do Gémeo Digital do Oceano da UE (OTD UE). Estas componentes regionais devem promover o desenvolvimento de aplicações locais de gémeos digitais: ferramentas digitais personalizadas concebidas para abordar as prioridades únicas de comunidades locais de partes interessadas específicas.

Para cada bacia marítima (um projeto por farol), o objetivo é:

  • Identificar, agregar e integrar os dados regionais existentes (através da EMODnet), as ferramentas, a modelização e os ativos digitais gémeos locais que ainda não são amplamente públicos (incluindo os ativos das águas interiores que são relevantes para a abordagem integrada fonte-mar, com destaque para as ligações terra-mar [1]) e tomar as medidas necessárias para os disponibilizar através do EDITO, seguindo todos os protocolos de interoperabilidade e normalização necessários. Os tipos de dados sub-representados (biologística, telemetria acústica, etc.) revestem-se de especial interesse;
  • Desenvolver serviços digitais gémeos regionais (aplicações e serviços adaptados que respondam aos desafios específicos de cada região, incluindo, por exemplo, os desafios das pequenas ilhas, a resiliência costeira, a conservação e restauração da biodiversidade, a poluição, a adaptação às alterações climáticas, as pescas e a aquicultura e outros setores da economia azul). Estes serviços devem visar tanto questões políticas relevantes como questões relacionadas com o desenvolvimento de uma economia azul regional sustentável e competitiva. A fim de apoiar as capacidades de previsão, o gémeo digital regional deve, em especial, procurar integrar conjuntos de dados ecológicos e de monitorização da biodiversidade a longo prazo, assegurando que a modelização e os cenários se baseiam em observações empíricas e em séries cronológicas;
  • Promover a participação das partes interessadas a nível regional (autoridades regionais, convenções marinhas regionais, parceiros industriais e comunidades locais) para integrar os ativos existentes (bases de dados, modelos locais ou regionais) na conceção conjunta e validação de aplicações digitais duplas para a elaboração de políticas eficazes e o apoio à tomada de decisões operacionais;
  • Melhorar a adoção intensiva de algoritmos inovadores de inteligência artificial e de gestão de megadados;
  • Através do compromisso acima referido, e através de processos de cocriação, desenvolver uma série de cenários "e se", avaliar os seus níveis de confiança e identificar ações para a melhoria da referida confiança.

[1] Por exemplo, ativos identificados no IDEATION CSA e financiados ao abrigo do «HORIZON-MISS-2023-OCEAN-01-09 towards the integration of inland waters into the Digital Twin Ocean». https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101157371

title: Facilitate the engagement of European stakeholders in international digital standardisation (CSA)
destinationDetails:
Through the European Partnership on Virtual Worlds, Europe will drive investment in advanced hardware, immersive interaction, and seamless integration across the Telco-Cloud-to-Edge continuum, enabling lifelike multisensory experiences and fully interoperable platforms. These efforts will enhance Europe’s capacity to innovate, deploy, and scale trustworthy virtual worlds, thereby strengthening competitiveness, resilience, and alignment with EU values.At the same time, a robust Web 4.0 architectural framework — underpinned by open-source solutions and shared standards — will be essential to ensure interoperability, decentralisation, and trust. By deepening Europe’s engagement in international digital standardisation, the Union will help shape global norms in line with its strategic interests, technological sovereignty, and core values.

Legal entities established in China are not eligible to participate in both Research and Innovation Actions (RIAs) and Innovation Actions (IAs) falling under this destination. For additional information please see “Restrictions on the participation of legal entities established in China” found in General Annex B of the General Annexes.
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

Proposals are expected to contribute to the following outcomes:

  • Increasing the participation and influence of European experts in digital standardisation to promote EU values and strategic interests, contributing to strengthen EU competitiveness in the digital field.
  • Improvement of the skills of European experts, especially from SMEs, R&I institutions, Open-Source community, academia and societal stakeholders, to successfully contribute and lead in the development of digital standards.
  • Development and update of standardisation landscapes and gap analyses of key digital technologies as outlined in the Rolling Plan for ICT Standardisation.
  • Provision of foresight analyses regarding standardisation in new emerging technologies to identify short and medium-term digital standardisation needs to support EU policies and anticipate appropriate participation by EU stakeholders.
  • More awareness of the benefits and competitive advantages of standardisation, in particular for SMEs and researchers, and more visibility of the European digital standardisation ecosystem.

Scope:

Contribute to the implementation of the EU Standardisation Strategy and other policy initiatives such as Europe’s Digital Decade, Apply AI Strategy or the Competitiveness Compass, with an emphasis on supporting the EU’s leading position in global standards-setting of key digital technologies.

The goals are inter alia to 1) strengthen the EU competitiveness in the digital domain; 2) contribute to EU tech sovereignty and 3) promote EU values and interests internationally, by empowering and financially supporting the active participation of European stakeholders in the development of digital international standards.

The objective is to reinforce the presence of experts from the EU and associated Horizon Europe countries in global digital standards setting, especially those coming from SMEs, R&I institutions, Open-Source community, academia and societal stakeholders.

To achieve this objective, proposals under this topic should provide for:

  • Setting up of a management facility to support contributions and leadership (e.g. chairing of technical committees, convenor positions) of European specialists in activities in relation to global digital standardisation
  • When relevant, support financially the hosting of international standardisation meetings (e.g. 3GPP, ISO/IEC JTC1) and workshops in Europe to ease the participation of European experts
  • Landscape and gap analysis of standardisation activities in key digital priority areas, as outlined in the Annual Union Work Programme and the Rolling Plan for ICT standardisation, including identification of new emerging technology areas.
  • Promotion of the relevance and benefits of digital standardisation, especially for strengthening the competitiveness of EU industry, driving sustainability, achieving tech sovereignty, and promoting EU values. The proposal shall build synergies with other similar EU- and national-funded initiatives. It shall also include actions, including development of tools and materials, to promote education and skills on standardisation.

Beneficiaries that intend to transfer ownership or grant an exclusive licence must formally notify the granting authority (i.e. DG-CNECT and HaDEA) before the intended transfer or licensing takes place and the granting authority may up to four years after the end of the action object to a transfer of ownership or the exclusive licensing of results.

The proposal should take into account the previous activities carried out at least in terms of educational material and facilities for funding experts within the topics ICT-40-2017 (implemented by the StandICT.eu project), ICT-45-2020 (implemented under StandICT.eu2023 project), HORIZON-CL4-2022-RESILIENCE-01-21 (implemented under StandICT.eu 2026) and HORIZON-CL4-2024-HUMAN-03-04 (implemented under StandICT.eu 2029).

See website: http://www.standict.eu.

Online Manual is your guide on the procedures from proposal submission to managing your grant.

Horizon Europe Programme Guide contains the detailed guidance to the structure, budget and political priorities of Horizon Europe.

Funding & Tenders Portal FAQ – find the answers to most frequently asked questions on submission of proposals, evaluation and grant management.

Research Enquiry Service – ask questions about any aspect of European research in general and the EU Research Framework Programmes in particular.

National Contact Points (NCPs) – get guidance, practical information and assistance on participation in Horizon Europe. There are also NCPs in many non-EU and non-associated countries (‘third-countries’).

Enterprise Europe Network – contact your EEN national contact for advice to businesses with special focus on SMEs. The support includes guidance on the EU research funding.

IT Helpdesk – contact the Funding & Tenders Portal IT helpdesk for questions such as forgotten passwords, access rights and roles, technical aspects of submission of proposals, etc.

European IPR Helpdesk assists you on intellectual property issues.

CEN-CENELEC Research Helpdesk and ETSI Research Helpdesk – the European Standards Organisations advise you how to tackle standardisation in your project proposal.

The European Charter for Researchers and the Code of Conduct for their recruitment – consult the general principles and requirements specifying the roles, responsibilities and entitlements of researchers, employers and funders of researchers.

Partner Search help you find a partner organisation for your proposal.

Condiciones generales

1. Condiciones de admisibilidad: Límite de página y diseño de la propuesta

Como se describe en los anexos A y E del Programa de Trabajo de Horizonte Europa, anexos generales.

Límites de página y diseño de la propuesta: descrito en la parte B del formulario de solicitud disponible en el sistema de presentación.

El límite de páginas para la Parte B de la aplicación de Investigación e Innovación (RIA) que utiliza la suma global es de 45 páginas. Además, es obligatorio presentar un cuadro presupuestario detallado, utilizando la plantilla disponible en el sistema de presentación.

2. Países elegibles

Como se describe en el anexo B de los anexos generales del programa de trabajo.

Varios países no pertenecientes a la UE o no asociados que no son automáticamente elegibles para recibir financiación han adoptado disposiciones específicas para poner fondos a disposición de sus participantes en proyectos de Horizonte Europa. Véase la información en la Guía del Programa Horizonte Europa.

3. Otras condiciones elegibles

El Centro Común de Investigación (CCI) podrá participar como miembro del consorcio seleccionado para recibir financiación como beneficiario sin financiación o como socio asociado. El CCI no participará en la preparación y presentación de la propuesta (véase el anexo general B).

Como se describe en el anexo B de los anexos generales del programa de trabajo.

4. Capacidad financiera y operativa y exclusión

Como se describe en el anexo C de los anexos generales del programa de trabajo.

5 bis. Evaluación y adjudicación: Criterios de adjudicación, puntuación y umbrales

Como se describe en el anexo D de los anexos generales del programa de trabajo.

5 ter. Evaluación y adjudicación: Procesos de presentación y evaluación

Tal como se describe en el anexo F de los anexos generales del programa de trabajo y en el Manual en línea.

5c. Evaluación y adjudicación: Calendario indicativo para la evaluación y el acuerdo de subvención

Como se describe en el anexo F de los anexos generales del programa de trabajo.

6. Estructura jurídica y financiera de las subvenciones

Los costes subvencionables adoptarán la forma de una cantidad a tanto alzado tal como se define en la Decisión de 7 de julio de 2021 por la que se autoriza el uso de contribuciones a tanto alzado en el marco del Programa Horizonte Europa —el Programa Marco de Investigación e Innovación (2021-2027)— y en las acciones del Programa de Investigación y Formación de la Comunidad Europea de la Energía Atómica (2021-2025) [[La presente Decisión está disponible en el Portal de Financiación y Licitaciones, en la sección de documentos de referencia de Horizonte Europa, en «Decisiones sobre costes simplificados» o a través del presente enlace: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/docs/2021-2027/horizon/guidance/ls-decision_he_en.pdf]].

La autoridad otorgante podrá, hasta cuatro años después de la finalización de la acción, oponerse a una transferencia de propiedad o a la concesión de licencias exclusivas de resultados, tal como se establece en la disposición específica del anexo 5.

Además, como se describe en el anexo G de los anexos generales del programa de trabajo.

title: La alfabetización digital y mediática como motores de la resiliencia democrática y cívica
destinationDetails:
El Estado de Derecho, el respeto de los derechos humanos y la democracia son valores fundamentales de la UE establecidos en el artículo 2 del Tratado de la Unión Europea. Estos valores proporcionan a la Unión orientaciones de principios para hacer frente a los inevitables cambios geopolíticos, económicos, sociales y demográficos que no podían preverse en el momento en que se redactaron los Tratados. Esto incluye cómo afectaría la transformación digital a la forma en que se configurarían el debate y los procesos políticos.

La democracia es una práctica cultural tanto como un sistema político. Es una fortaleza clave de las sociedades europeas, ya que contribuye a garantizar el respeto de la igualdad, el Estado de Derecho, los derechos fundamentales y la libertad. Los actores con tendencias antidemocráticas atacan a las democracias y sus instituciones porque la democracia es una salvaguardia contra ellas[[[El informe de 2025 del Instituto V-Dem («¿25 años de autocratización-democracia triunfaron?»)] confirma las terribles señales, indicadores y tendencias capturados en años anteriores de medición: «La tendencia de la «tercera ola de autocratización» se está profundizando y extendiendo. Esto incluye el debilitamiento de la democracia en algunas democracias liberales establecidas, la ruptura de la democracia en países que fueron democráticos durante la mayor parte del siglo XXI, así como la profundización de la autocracia en estados ya autocráticos […] El declive democrático mundial se profundiza, independientemente de cómo dividamos los datos y de la medida que usemos» (pp. 9 y 10)]]. Incluso las democracias que tradicionalmente funcionan bien se enfrentan a muchos desafíos, lo que significa que también necesitan adaptarse continuamente a medida que cambian las condiciones. La investigación en ciencias sociales y humanidades (SSH) desempeña un papel crucial en la comprensión de los desafíos y amenazas actuales y en el mapeo de las vías futuras para soluciones innovadoras. Sobre la base de perspectivas históricas, culturales, sociales, jurídicas y filosóficas, la investigación fomentará un mayor desarrollo de la democracia con vistas a mejorar la participación ciudadana y la elaboración de políticas inclusivas, promover la igualdad y la inclusión, abordar el impacto de la IA y la transformación digital de la democracia. También reforzará la resiliencia democrática y la preparación cívica, y preservará el papel de los medios de comunicación libres, independientes y plurales como principios clave de la democracia, entre otros objetivos.

Impacto previsto:

Las propuestas de temas en el marco de este destino deben establecer una vía creíble para contribuir al siguiente impacto previsto del plan estratégico de Horizonte Europa:

  • Revigorizar la gobernanza democrática mediante la mejora de la independencia, la rendición de cuentas, la transparencia, la eficacia y la fiabilidad de las instituciones y las políticas basadas en el Estado de Derecho, y mediante la ampliación de la participación y el compromiso activos e inclusivos de los ciudadanos, potenciados por la salvaguardia de los derechos fundamentales.

El objetivo de la inversión en investigación que respalda este impacto es desarrollar una base empírica sólida que pueda servir de base para el establecimiento de políticas eficaces, pertinentes y sensatas, que refuercen la resiliencia de los sistemas democráticos y los protejan de las amenazas. Al mismo tiempo, busca fomentar el pensamiento crítico al tiempo que refuerza la confianza de los ciudadanos en la democracia, sus instituciones y el sentido de participación política en su sentido más amplio posible.

El destino busca sinergias con otros programas pertinentes de la UE, en particular para la adopción de los resultados de la investigación y las soluciones innovadoras desarrolladas en el marco de Horizonte Europa. Se fomenta la interacción, entre otros, con los siguientes programas: Europa Digital (DIGITAL), Instrumento de Apoyo Técnico, CERV (Ciudadanos, Igualdad, Derechos y Valores), Erasmus+, FSE+ y Europa Global: Instrumento de Vecindad, Desarrollo y Cooperación Internacional.

Se anima a los solicitantes a considerar, cuando proceda, los servicios ofrecidos por las infraestructuras de investigación europeas actuales y futuras financiadas por la UE, en particular las del ámbito de las ciencias sociales y las humanidades [1]. Cuando proceda, las propuestas deben aprovechar los datos y servicios disponibles a través de las infraestructuras de investigación europeas federadas en el marco de la Nube Europea de la Ciencia Abierta, así como los datos de los espacios de datos pertinentes.

Dado que el destino apunta directamente a la participación ciudadana y a producir un cambio duradero, es de particular importancia que las acciones de investigación e innovación promuevan los más altos estándares de transparencia y apertura. Deben realizarse esfuerzos especiales para garantizar que los datos producidos en el contexto de este destino sean FAIR (encontrables, accesibles, interoperables y reutilizables). Cuando proceda, se anima a abrir el proceso, los criterios, las metodologías y los datos a la sociedad civil en el transcurso de la investigación.

Para maximizar el impacto de la I+D+i en este Destino en consonancia con las prioridades de la UE, se fomenta la cooperación internacional siempre que sea pertinente en los temas propuestos.

[1] Para una lista completa, véase https://ri-portfolio.esfri.eu/ri-portfolio/table. En el ámbito de las ciencias sociales, véase, por ejemplo: CESSDA - Consortium of European Social Science Data Archives (https://www.cessda.eu/), ESS – European Social Survey (https://www.europeansocialsurvey.org/), SHARE - Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (https://www.share-eric.eu/) o la Infraestructura Europea de Investigación sobre el Holocausto (https://ehri-project.eu/)

descriptionByte:
Resultado esperado:

Los proyectos deben contribuir a todos los siguientes resultados esperados:

  • Las instituciones de la UE y los responsables nacionales de la toma de decisiones tienen una mejor comprensión de cómo fomentar la resiliencia democrática a través de la alfabetización mediática y digital, equipando a las sociedades para adaptarse y prosperar frente a la evolución de los desafíos tecnológicos, políticos y sociales.
  • Los ciudadanos están facultados para navegar por el panorama digital con discernimiento y pensamiento crítico, participando activamente con los medios de comunicación y otras fuentes de información, garantizando una participación democrática informada.

Ámbito de aplicación:

Como se recuerda en el informe «Safer together»[1], «en los últimos años, la Comisión ya ha tomado medidas para luchar contra las amenazas híbridas (incluida la manipulación de información e injerencia extranjeras/IFMI) y mejorar la resiliencia democrática en toda la UE. Adoptó, entre otras iniciativas, el Plan de Acción para la Democracia Europea [2] para construir democracias más resilientes en toda la UE mediante la promoción de elecciones libres y justas, el refuerzo de la libertad de los medios de comunicación, la lucha contra la desinformación y la manipulación de información e injerencia por parte de agentes extranjeros y la promoción de la integridad de la información. Con la adopción de la Ley de Servicios Digitales [3] y sus obligaciones vinculantes para las plataformas en línea de luchar contra la difusión de desinformación, la Comisión también reforzó el Código de Buenas Prácticas en materia de Desinformación, que se convirtió en un Código de Conducta en el marco de la Ley de Servicios Digitales. Además, la puesta en marcha del Observatorio Europeo de los Medios de Comunicación Digitales (EDMO) y sus centros aumentaron la capacidad de detectar, analizar y exponer campañas de desinformación».[4]

La Estrategia de la Unión de Preparación [5] subraya que la preparación es una responsabilidad colectiva. También señala la necesidad de aumentar la resiliencia de nuestras democracias, en particular con vistas a reforzar la confianza en las instituciones, que puede ser crucial en situaciones de crisis, como se ha visto, por ejemplo, durante la pandemia de COVID-19. Los grupos que se encuentran en una situación vulnerable en particular, como los niños, las personas mayores y las personas con discapacidad, las minorías étnicas o religiosas, las personas LGBTIQ, las personas que sufren pobreza o exclusión social, se ven afectados de manera desproporcionada por las crisis, lo que a menudo exacerba las desventajas, barreras y desigualdades preexistentes.

La desinformación es especialmente perjudicial, ya que socava la confianza pública y puede exacerbar el impacto de las crisis. Los ciudadanos comprometidos, informados y empoderados son la mejor garantía para la resiliencia de nuestras democracias. Las autoridades públicas, las escuelas, las universidades y las instituciones de formación, las iniciativas juveniles, las organizaciones y asociaciones de la sociedad civil, los interlocutores sociales, las empresas, las redes y comunidades locales y los ciudadanos desde una edad temprana desempeñan un papel vital en este esfuerzo colectivo, y la investigación propuesta debe adoptar un enfoque multiactor.

En este contexto, la investigación propuesta debe explorar los patrones complejos y dinámicos de los comportamientos de los usuarios en la era digital, investigando cómo las personas buscan, evalúan e interactúan con la información en línea y fuera de línea. Tal exploración se beneficiará de incluir un análisis de la dinámica emocional en la difusión de desinformación y polarización en plataformas digitales. Esto es especialmente relevante en contextos de crisis en los que la manipulación de la información y la desinformación extranjeras pueden aprovecharse para aumentar el pánico y la confusión. Las propuestas deben investigar cómo los algoritmos amplifican el contenido emotivo, fomentando la polarización y socavando la confianza en las instituciones democráticas, así como la respuesta a las crisis y desarrollar estrategias digitales y de alfabetización mediática para contrarrestar narrativas emocionalmente manipuladoras, como los discursos populistas y posteriores a la verdad.

La investigación también debe examinar los factores que influyen en la alfabetización digital, los hábitos de búsqueda de información y el compromiso en línea, centrándose en mejorar la participación y el compromiso de los ciudadanos a través de medios digitales (también a través de la tecnología cívica) y la toma de decisiones informada. En un momento en que la desinformación se utiliza para sembrar la discordia explotando los temores de los ciudadanos, es crucial garantizar que las decisiones democráticas se basen en los hechos y las fuentes de información disponibles más fiables y ampliamente aceptados. La investigación debe explorar el papel fundamental que puede desempeñar la alfabetización digital y mediática en el fomento de la resiliencia social y la integridad de la información, permitiendo a los ciudadanos navegar y resistir la desinformación y la desinformación.

Las propuestas deben planificar una evaluación crítica de las iniciativas de alfabetización mediática y digital [6] para evaluar si los esfuerzos existentes están mejorando la resiliencia de los ciudadanos o si se necesitan nuevos enfoques para equipar más eficazmente a los ciudadanos contra la evolución de las tácticas de manipulación.

La investigación debe identificar estrategias para mejorar la alfabetización mediática y la alfabetización digital y mediática, con el fin de mejorar el pensamiento crítico, promover la toma de decisiones basada en pruebas y contrarrestar los efectos negativos de la desinformación en las sociedades democráticas. Para facilitar la generación de soluciones prácticas para educadores y responsables políticos, la investigación podría utilizar herramientas computacionales, como el análisis de redes sociales y el procesamiento del lenguaje natural, para mapear y mitigar la difusión de desinformación en múltiples plataformas. Esto incluye identificar el Comportamiento Inauthentic Coordinado y analizar el contenido textual y visual para informar las iniciativas de alfabetización mediática.

Se anima a las propuestas a identificar otros proyectos pertinentes financiados por la UE relacionados con la alfabetización mediática y digital, y a explorar posibles oportunidades de colaboración con ellos. Se recomienda encarecidamente la agrupación y la cooperación con otros proyectos seleccionados en relación con este tema y otros proyectos pertinentes.

Se anima a los proyectos seleccionados para su financiación a que colaboren con el CCI para buscar sinergias con su trabajo en materia de innovación para la democracia y la gobernanza pública.

Funding & Tenders Portal FAQ: encuentra las respuestas a las preguntas más frecuentes sobre la presentación de propuestas, la evaluación y la gestión de subvenciones.

Servicio de Investigación: formular preguntas sobre cualquier aspecto de la investigación europea en general y de los programas marco de investigación de la UE en particular.

Puntos de contacto nacionales (PCN): obtener orientación, información práctica y asistencia sobre la participación en Horizonte Europa. También hay puntos de contacto nacionales en muchos países no pertenecientes a la UE y no asociados («terceros países»).

Red Europea para las Empresas: póngase en contacto con su contacto nacional de la Red Europea para las Empresas para asesorar a las empresas, prestando especial atención a las pymes. El apoyo incluye orientaciones sobre la financiación de la investigación de la UE.

European IPR Helpdesk le ayuda en cuestiones de propiedad intelectual.

CEN-CENELEC Research Helpdesk y ETSI Research Helpdesk: las organizaciones europeas de normalización le aconsejan cómo abordar la normalización en su propuesta de proyecto.

La Carta Europea del Investigador y el Código de Conducta para su contratación: consulta los principios y requisitos generales que especifican las funciones, responsabilidades y derechos de los investigadores, los empleadores y los financiadores de los investigadores.

title: Facilitate the engagement of European stakeholders in international digital standardisation (CSA)
destinationDetails:
Through the European Partnership on Virtual Worlds, Europe will drive investment in advanced hardware, immersive interaction, and seamless integration across the Telco-Cloud-to-Edge continuum, enabling lifelike multisensory experiences and fully interoperable platforms. These efforts will enhance Europe’s capacity to innovate, deploy, and scale trustworthy virtual worlds, thereby strengthening competitiveness, resilience, and alignment with EU values.At the same time, a robust Web 4.0 architectural framework — underpinned by open-source solutions and shared standards — will be essential to ensure interoperability, decentralisation, and trust. By deepening Europe’s engagement in international digital standardisation, the Union will help shape global norms in line with its strategic interests, technological sovereignty, and core values.

Legal entities established in China are not eligible to participate in both Research and Innovation Actions (RIAs) and Innovation Actions (IAs) falling under this destination. For additional information please see “Restrictions on the participation of legal entities established in China” found in General Annex B of the General Annexes.
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

Proposals are expected to contribute to the following outcomes:

  • Increasing the participation and influence of European experts in digital standardisation to promote EU values and strategic interests, contributing to strengthen EU competitiveness in the digital field.
  • Improvement of the skills of European experts, especially from SMEs, R&I institutions, Open-Source community, academia and societal stakeholders, to successfully contribute and lead in the development of digital standards.
  • Development and update of standardisation landscapes and gap analyses of key digital technologies as outlined in the Rolling Plan for ICT Standardisation.
  • Provision of foresight analyses regarding standardisation in new emerging technologies to identify short and medium-term digital standardisation needs to support EU policies and anticipate appropriate participation by EU stakeholders.
  • More awareness of the benefits and competitive advantages of standardisation, in particular for SMEs and researchers, and more visibility of the European digital standardisation ecosystem.

Scope:

Contribute to the implementation of the EU Standardisation Strategy and other policy initiatives such as Europe’s Digital Decade, Apply AI Strategy or the Competitiveness Compass, with an emphasis on supporting the EU’s leading position in global standards-setting of key digital technologies.

The goals are inter alia to 1) strengthen the EU competitiveness in the digital domain; 2) contribute to EU tech sovereignty and 3) promote EU values and interests internationally, by empowering and financially supporting the active participation of European stakeholders in the development of digital international standards.

The objective is to reinforce the presence of experts from the EU and associated Horizon Europe countries in global digital standards setting, especially those coming from SMEs, R&I institutions, Open-Source community, academia and societal stakeholders.

To achieve this objective, proposals under this topic should provide for:

  • Setting up of a management facility to support contributions and leadership (e.g. chairing of technical committees, convenor positions) of European specialists in activities in relation to global digital standardisation
  • When relevant, support financially the hosting of international standardisation meetings (e.g. 3GPP, ISO/IEC JTC1) and workshops in Europe to ease the participation of European experts
  • Landscape and gap analysis of standardisation activities in key digital priority areas, as outlined in the Annual Union Work Programme and the Rolling Plan for ICT standardisation, including identification of new emerging technology areas.
  • Promotion of the relevance and benefits of digital standardisation, especially for strengthening the competitiveness of EU industry, driving sustainability, achieving tech sovereignty, and promoting EU values. The proposal shall build synergies with other similar EU- and national-funded initiatives. It shall also include actions, including development of tools and materials, to promote education and skills on standardisation.

Beneficiaries that intend to transfer ownership or grant an exclusive licence must formally notify the granting authority (i.e. DG-CNECT and HaDEA) before the intended transfer or licensing takes place and the granting authority may up to four years after the end of the action object to a transfer of ownership or the exclusive licensing of results.

The proposal should take into account the previous activities carried out at least in terms of educational material and facilities for funding experts within the topics ICT-40-2017 (implemented by the StandICT.eu project), ICT-45-2020 (implemented under StandICT.eu2023 project), HORIZON-CL4-2022-RESILIENCE-01-21 (implemented under StandICT.eu 2026) and HORIZON-CL4-2024-HUMAN-03-04 (implemented under StandICT.eu 2029).

See website: http://www.standict.eu.

Beneficiaries may provide financial support to third parties (FSTP). The support to third parties can only be provided in the form of grants. As the primary purpose of the action is to support European experts in the global ICT standardisation scene, a minimum of 75% of the total requested EU contribution should be allocated to FSTP selected through open calls. title: Facilitate the engagement of European stakeholders in international digital standardisation (CSA)
destinationDetails:
Through the European Partnership on Virtual Worlds, Europe will drive investment in advanced hardware, immersive interaction, and seamless integration across the Telco-Cloud-to-Edge continuum, enabling lifelike multisensory experiences and fully interoperable platforms. These efforts will enhance Europe’s capacity to innovate, deploy, and scale trustworthy virtual worlds, thereby strengthening competitiveness, resilience, and alignment with EU values.At the same time, a robust Web 4.0 architectural framework — underpinned by open-source solutions and shared standards — will be essential to ensure interoperability, decentralisation, and trust. By deepening Europe’s engagement in international digital standardisation, the Union will help shape global norms in line with its strategic interests, technological sovereignty, and core values.

Legal entities established in China are not eligible to participate in both Research and Innovation Actions (RIAs) and Innovation Actions (IAs) falling under this destination. For additional information please see “Restrictions on the participation of legal entities established in China” found in General Annex B of the General Annexes.
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

Proposals are expected to contribute to the following outcomes:

  • Increasing the participation and influence of European experts in digital standardisation to promote EU values and strategic interests, contributing to strengthen EU competitiveness in the digital field.
  • Improvement of the skills of European experts, especially from SMEs, R&I institutions, Open-Source community, academia and societal stakeholders, to successfully contribute and lead in the development of digital standards.
  • Development and update of standardisation landscapes and gap analyses of key digital technologies as outlined in the Rolling Plan for ICT Standardisation.
  • Provision of foresight analyses regarding standardisation in new emerging technologies to identify short and medium-term digital standardisation needs to support EU policies and anticipate appropriate participation by EU stakeholders.
  • More awareness of the benefits and competitive advantages of standardisation, in particular for SMEs and researchers, and more visibility of the European digital standardisation ecosystem.

Scope:

Contribute to the implementation of the EU Standardisation Strategy and other policy initiatives such as Europe’s Digital Decade, Apply AI Strategy or the Competitiveness Compass, with an emphasis on supporting the EU’s leading position in global standards-setting of key digital technologies.

The goals are inter alia to 1) strengthen the EU competitiveness in the digital domain; 2) contribute to EU tech sovereignty and 3) promote EU values and interests internationally, by empowering and financially supporting the active participation of European stakeholders in the development of digital international standards.

The objective is to reinforce the presence of experts from the EU and associated Horizon Europe countries in global digital standards setting, especially those coming from SMEs, R&I institutions, Open-Source community, academia and societal stakeholders.

To achieve this objective, proposals under this topic should provide for:

  • Setting up of a management facility to support contributions and leadership (e.g. chairing of technical committees, convenor positions) of European specialists in activities in relation to global digital standardisation
  • When relevant, support financially the hosting of international standardisation meetings (e.g. 3GPP, ISO/IEC JTC1) and workshops in Europe to ease the participation of European experts
  • Landscape and gap analysis of standardisation activities in key digital priority areas, as outlined in the Annual Union Work Programme and the Rolling Plan for ICT standardisation, including identification of new emerging technology areas.
  • Promotion of the relevance and benefits of digital standardisation, especially for strengthening the competitiveness of EU industry, driving sustainability, achieving tech sovereignty, and promoting EU values. The proposal shall build synergies with other similar EU- and national-funded initiatives. It shall also include actions, including development of tools and materials, to promote education and skills on standardisation.

Beneficiaries that intend to transfer ownership or grant an exclusive licence must formally notify the granting authority (i.e. DG-CNECT and HaDEA) before the intended transfer or licensing takes place and the granting authority may up to four years after the end of the action object to a transfer of ownership or the exclusive licensing of results.

The proposal should take into account the previous activities carried out at least in terms of educational material and facilities for funding experts within the topics ICT-40-2017 (implemented by the StandICT.eu project), ICT-45-2020 (implemented under StandICT.eu2023 project), HORIZON-CL4-2022-RESILIENCE-01-21 (implemented under StandICT.eu 2026) and HORIZON-CL4-2024-HUMAN-03-04 (implemented under StandICT.eu 2029).

See website: http://www.standict.eu.

descriptionByte:
Rezultatul preconizat:

Accentul trebuie pus pe domeniile în care țările din cadrul parteneriatului digital oferă expertiză complementară solidă, inclusiv ambalaje avansate, integrare eterogenă și tehnologii ale cipurilor fotonice. Tema ar urmări să încurajeze colaborarea dintre comunitățile de cercetare și inovare din țările Parteneriatului european și din țările Parteneriatului digital. Se preconizează că proiectele vor contribui la următoarele rezultate:

• Concepte inovatoare de proiectare și integrare pentru sistemele informatice neuromorfe care sprijină consumul foarte scăzut de energie, conectivitatea, funcțiile integrate pentru aplicațiile mobile.

• Tehnologii alternative de proces de fabricație pentru cipurile semiconductoare, inclusiv front-end sau back-end pentru integrarea eterogenă. Tehnologiile ar trebui să susțină pe termen mediu și lung evoluția rapidă a performanței, miniaturizării și costurilor dispozitivelor, reducând în același timp amprenta de mediu.

• Soluții de ambalare foarte avansate care vizează integrarea eterogenă a mai multor funcții și materiale pentru aplicații în comunicare (RF, mmW sau THz), detecție, acționare, gestionare a puterii și integrare activă/pasivă.

Serviciul de informare în domeniul cercetării – adresați întrebări cu privire la orice aspect al cercetării europene în general și al programelor-cadru de cercetare ale UE în special.

Punctele naționale de contact (PCN) – obțineți orientări, informații practice și asistență cu privire la participarea la programul Orizont Europa. Există, de asemenea, puncte de contact naționale în multe țări din afara UE și țări neasociate („țări terțe”).

Rețeaua întreprinderilor europene – contactați contactul național EEN pentru consilierea întreprinderilor, cu un accent special pe IMM-uri. Sprijinul include orientări privind finanțarea cercetării de către UE.
