title: Secure PQC implementations, Cryptanalysis and Post-quantum Digital Trust
callTitle: Indirectly Managed Action by the ECCC (2027)
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

Proposals are expected to contribute one or more of the following:

  • Practical robust implementations of PQC schemes that can withstand implementation attacks including side-channel attacks, fault attacks and combined attacks, and design of automated tools for evaluating the security of PQC implementations. Comprehensive guidelines for implementing countermeasures against a wide range of attacks;
  • Advances in understanding the quantum hardness of mathematical problem classes; new quantum algorithms and improvements in quantum programming and implementation; security validation methods; design of post-quantum schemes with improved security against quantum and AI-based attacks;
  • Post-quantum schemes and protocols to support privacy-friendly applications and services, ncluding the secure and private use of electronic identities. Design of new digital signatures, key encapsulation mechanisms, and other schemes or use of existing ones to build new verification protocols.

Scope:

Securing PQC algorithm implementations is vital to protect against implementation attacks, such as side channel attacks, fault attacks and combinations of these, which may be amplified by deep learning. Current countermeasures incur significant overhead, and new approaches are needed to balance security and performance. Formal verification tools and methodologies can help achieve this goal and provide machine-readable evidence. Furthermore, to boost confidence in PQC systems, their security should be assessed, including the potential impact of new quantum algorithms or new optimizations of existing ones, also combined with AI.

Another key research area is digital trust in the post-quantum era, which requires transforming various areas, such as secure identities, data protection, access to essential services, and applications such as backup recovery, browser extensions and others into trusted and reliable solutions, via new post-quantum schemes and advanced building blocks for privacy-enhancing protocols.

Proposals should address one of the following technology areas:

  • Development of solutions to prevent implementation attacks, balancing security, performance and cost; research in new attacks, including AI-powered ones, and/or combination of attacks, to inform secure design; creation of testing frameworks for automated security evaluations; improvement of formal verification methodologies.
  • Quantum hardness analysis, via the study of the impact of new quantum algorithms or improvement of existing quantum algorithm implementations as well as the impact of AI-supported quantum attacks; analysis of cryptanalysis results; design of new post-quantum schemes using the information of the advances achieved/ fine-tuning of parameters sets.
  • Design of quantum-resistant schemes and protocols supporting the field of privacy-friendly applications and services, including electronic identities, verification protocols and pseudonymous access options, protocols for attestation and anonymous attestation, for real world scenarios, via the design of new digital signature schemes and key encapsulation mechanisms, design of advanced cryptographic schemes, and usage of existing schemes in new protocols, for post-quantum digital identity and digital trust systems.

title: Facilitate the engagement of European stakeholders in international digital standardisation (CSA)
destinationDetails:
Through the European Partnership on Virtual Worlds, Europe will drive investment in advanced hardware, immersive interaction, and seamless integration across the Telco-Cloud-to-Edge continuum, enabling lifelike multisensory experiences and fully interoperable platforms. These efforts will enhance Europe’s capacity to innovate, deploy, and scale trustworthy virtual worlds, thereby strengthening competitiveness, resilience, and alignment with EU values.At the same time, a robust Web 4.0 architectural framework — underpinned by open-source solutions and shared standards — will be essential to ensure interoperability, decentralisation, and trust. By deepening Europe’s engagement in international digital standardisation, the Union will help shape global norms in line with its strategic interests, technological sovereignty, and core values.

Legal entities established in China are not eligible to participate in both Research and Innovation Actions (RIAs) and Innovation Actions (IAs) falling under this destination. For additional information please see “Restrictions on the participation of legal entities established in China” found in General Annex B of the General Annexes.
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

Proposals are expected to contribute to the following outcomes:

  • Increasing the participation and influence of European experts in digital standardisation to promote EU values and strategic interests, contributing to strengthen EU competitiveness in the digital field.
  • Improvement of the skills of European experts, especially from SMEs, R&I institutions, Open-Source community, academia and societal stakeholders, to successfully contribute and lead in the development of digital standards.
  • Development and update of standardisation landscapes and gap analyses of key digital technologies as outlined in the Rolling Plan for ICT Standardisation.
  • Provision of foresight analyses regarding standardisation in new emerging technologies to identify short and medium-term digital standardisation needs to support EU policies and anticipate appropriate participation by EU stakeholders.
  • More awareness of the benefits and competitive advantages of standardisation, in particular for SMEs and researchers, and more visibility of the European digital standardisation ecosystem.

Scope:

Contribute to the implementation of the EU Standardisation Strategy and other policy initiatives such as Europe’s Digital Decade, Apply AI Strategy or the Competitiveness Compass, with an emphasis on supporting the EU’s leading position in global standards-setting of key digital technologies.

The goals are inter alia to 1) strengthen the EU competitiveness in the digital domain; 2) contribute to EU tech sovereignty and 3) promote EU values and interests internationally, by empowering and financially supporting the active participation of European stakeholders in the development of digital international standards.

The objective is to reinforce the presence of experts from the EU and associated Horizon Europe countries in global digital standards setting, especially those coming from SMEs, R&I institutions, Open-Source community, academia and societal stakeholders.

To achieve this objective, proposals under this topic should provide for:

  • Setting up of a management facility to support contributions and leadership (e.g. chairing of technical committees, convenor positions) of European specialists in activities in relation to global digital standardisation
  • When relevant, support financially the hosting of international standardisation meetings (e.g. 3GPP, ISO/IEC JTC1) and workshops in Europe to ease the participation of European experts
  • Landscape and gap analysis of standardisation activities in key digital priority areas, as outlined in the Annual Union Work Programme and the Rolling Plan for ICT standardisation, including identification of new emerging technology areas.
  • Promotion of the relevance and benefits of digital standardisation, especially for strengthening the competitiveness of EU industry, driving sustainability, achieving tech sovereignty, and promoting EU values. The proposal shall build synergies with other similar EU- and national-funded initiatives. It shall also include actions, including development of tools and materials, to promote education and skills on standardisation.

Beneficiaries that intend to transfer ownership or grant an exclusive licence must formally notify the granting authority (i.e. DG-CNECT and HaDEA) before the intended transfer or licensing takes place and the granting authority may up to four years after the end of the action object to a transfer of ownership or the exclusive licensing of results.

The proposal should take into account the previous activities carried out at least in terms of educational material and facilities for funding experts within the topics ICT-40-2017 (implemented by the StandICT.eu project), ICT-45-2020 (implemented under StandICT.eu2023 project), HORIZON-CL4-2022-RESILIENCE-01-21 (implemented under StandICT.eu 2026) and HORIZON-CL4-2024-HUMAN-03-04 (implemented under StandICT.eu 2029).

See website: http://www.standict.eu.

Condições gerais

Limites da página da proposta e apresentação: descritas na parte B do formulário de candidatura disponível no sistema de apresentação de candidaturas.

title: A literacia digital e mediática como motores da resiliência democrática e cívica
destinationDetails:
O Estado de direito, o respeito pelos direitos humanos e a democracia são valores fundamentais da UE consagrados no artigo 2.o do Tratado da União Europeia. Estes valores proporcionam à União orientações baseadas em princípios para fazer face às inevitáveis alterações geopolíticas económicas, sociais e demográficas que não podiam ser previstas aquando da elaboração dos Tratados. Tal inclui a forma como a transformação digital afetaria a forma como o debate e os processos políticos seriam moldados.

A democracia é uma prática cultural, tanto quanto um sistema político. Trata-se de uma força fundamental das sociedades europeias, que contribui para garantir o respeito pela igualdade, pelo Estado de direito, pelos direitos fundamentais e pela liberdade. Os intervenientes com tendências antidemocráticas atacam as democracias e as suas instituições porque a democracia é uma salvaguarda contra elas [[O relatório de 2025 do Instituto V-Dem («25 anos de Autocratização-Democracia Trumped?») confirma os terríveis sinais, indicadores e tendências captados ao longo dos anos de medição anteriores: «A tendência da «terceira vaga de autocratização» está a aprofundar-se e a propagar-se. Tal inclui o enfraquecimento da democracia em algumas democracias liberais estabelecidas, o colapso da democracia em países que foram democráticos durante a maior parte do século XXI, bem como o aprofundamento da autocracia em Estados já autocráticos […] O declínio democrático mundial aprofunda-se, independentemente da forma como cortamos os dados e da medida que utilizamos» (pp. 9 e 10)]]. Mesmo as democracias que tradicionalmente funcionam bem enfrentam muitos desafios, o que significa que também têm de se adaptar continuamente à medida que as condições mudam. A investigação em ciências sociais e humanas (CSH) desempenha um papel crucial na compreensão dos desafios e ameaças atuais e no mapeamento de vias futuras para soluções inovadoras. Com base em perspetivas históricas, culturais, sociais, jurídicas e filosóficas, a investigação promoverá um maior desenvolvimento da democracia, com vista a reforçar a participação dos cidadãos e a elaboração de políticas inclusivas, promovendo a igualdade e a inclusividade, abordando o impacto da IA e a transformação digital da democracia. Reforçará igualmente a resiliência democrática e a preparação cívica e preservará o papel dos meios de comunicação social livres, independentes e plurais como princípios fundamentais da democracia, entre outros objetivos.

Impacto esperado:

As propostas de temas no âmbito deste destino devem definir uma via credível para contribuir para o seguinte impacto esperado do Plano Estratégico do Horizonte Europa:

  • Reforçando a governação democrática, melhorando a independência, a responsabilização, a transparência, a eficácia e a fiabilidade das instituições e das políticas baseadas no Estado de direito, e através do alargamento da participação e do envolvimento ativos e inclusivos dos cidadãos, capacitados pela salvaguarda dos direitos fundamentais.

O objetivo do investimento em investigação que apoia este impacto é desenvolver uma base factual sólida que possa contribuir para o estabelecimento de políticas eficazes, pertinentes e sensatas, que reforcem a resiliência dos sistemas democráticos e os protejam das ameaças. Ao mesmo tempo, procura promover o pensamento crítico, reforçando simultaneamente a confiança dos cidadãos na democracia, nas suas instituições e no sentido mais amplo possível da participação política.

O destino procura sinergias com outros programas pertinentes da UE, em especial para a adoção dos resultados da investigação e das soluções inovadoras desenvolvidas no âmbito do Horizonte Europa. É incentivada a interação, nomeadamente, com os seguintes programas: Europa Digital (DIGITAL), Instrumento de Assistência Técnica, CIDV (Cidadãos, Igualdade, Direitos e Valores), Erasmus+, FSE+ e Europa Global: Instrumento de Vizinhança, de Cooperação para o Desenvolvimento e de Cooperação Internacional.

Os candidatos são incentivados a considerar, se for caso disso, os serviços oferecidos pelas atuais e futuras infraestruturas de investigação europeias financiadas pela UE, em especial no domínio das ciências sociais e humanas [1]. Se for caso disso, as propostas devem tirar partido dos dados e serviços disponíveis através das infraestruturas de investigação europeias federadas ao abrigo da Nuvem Europeia para a Ciência Aberta, bem como dos dados dos espaços de dados pertinentes.

Uma vez que o destino visa diretamente a participação dos cidadãos e a produção de mudanças duradouras, é particularmente importante que as ações de investigação e inovação promovam os mais elevados padrões de transparência e abertura. Devem ser envidados esforços especiais para garantir que os dados produzidos no contexto deste destino sejam FAIR (Encontráveis, Acessíveis, Interoperáveis e Reutilizáveis). Quando aplicável, incentiva-se a abertura do processo, dos critérios, das metodologias e dos dados à sociedade civil no decurso da investigação.

A fim de maximizar os impactos da I&I no âmbito deste destino, em consonância com as prioridades da UE, incentiva-se a cooperação internacional sempre que pertinente nos temas propostos.

[1] Para uma lista completa, ver https://ri-portfolio.esfri.eu/ri-portfolio/table. No domínio das ciências sociais, ver, por exemplo: CESSDA – Consórcio de Arquivos Europeus de Dados de Ciências Sociais (https://www.cessda.eu/), ESS – Inquérito Social Europeu (https://www.europeansocialsurvey.org/), SHARE – Inquérito sobre Saúde, Envelhecimento e Reforma na Europa (https://www.share-eric.eu/ ) ou Infraestrutura Europeia de Investigação sobre o Holocausto (https://ehri-project.eu/)

descriptionByte:
Resultado esperado:

Os projetos devem contribuir para todos os seguintes resultados esperados:

  • As instituições da UE e os decisores nacionais têm uma melhor compreensão de como promover a resiliência democrática através da literacia mediática e digital, dotando as sociedades de meios para se adaptarem e prosperarem face à evolução dos desafios tecnológicos, políticos e societais.
  • Os cidadãos estão capacitados para navegar no panorama digital com discernimento e pensamento crítico, colaborando ativamente com os meios de comunicação social e outras fontes de informação, assegurando uma participação democrática informada.

Âmbito de aplicação:

Tal como recordado no relatório «Safer together»[1], «nos últimos anos, a Comissão já tomou medidas para combater as ameaças híbridas (incluindo a manipulação da informação e ingerência por parte de agentes estrangeiros/FIMI) e reforçar a resiliência democrática em toda a UE. Adotou, entre outras iniciativas, o Plano de Ação para a Democracia Europeia [2] para construir democracias mais resilientes em toda a UE, promovendo eleições livres e justas, reforçando a liberdade dos meios de comunicação social, combatendo a desinformação e a FIMI e promovendo a integridade da informação. Com a adoção do Regulamento dos Serviços Digitais [3] e as suas obrigações vinculativas para as plataformas em linha no sentido de combater a propagação da desinformação, a Comissão reforçou igualmente o Código de Conduta sobre Desinformação, que se tornou um código de conduta no âmbito do Regulamento dos Serviços Digitais. Além disso, o lançamento do Observatório Europeu dos Meios de Comunicação Digitais (EDMO) e dos seus polos aumentou a capacidade de detetar, analisar e expor campanhas de desinformação.»[4]

A Estratégia para a União da Preparação [5] sublinha que a preparação é uma responsabilidade coletiva. Salienta igualmente a necessidade de tornar as nossas democracias mais resilientes, em especial com vista a reforçar a confiança nas instituições, o que pode ser crucial em situações de crise, como se verificou, por exemplo, durante a pandemia de COVID-19. Os grupos em situação vulnerável, em particular, como as crianças, os idosos e as pessoas com deficiência, as minorias étnicas ou religiosas, as pessoas LGBTIQ, as pessoas em situação de pobreza e/ou exclusão social, são desproporcionadamente afetados por crises, agravando frequentemente as desvantagens, os obstáculos e as desigualdades preexistentes.

A desinformação é particularmente prejudicial, uma vez que mina a confiança do público e pode agravar o impacto das crises. Cidadãos empenhados, informados e capacitados são a melhor garantia para a resiliência das nossas democracias. As autoridades públicas, as escolas, as universidades e as instituições de formação, as iniciativas de juventude, as organizações e associações da sociedade civil, os parceiros sociais, as empresas, as redes e comunidades locais e os cidadãos desde tenra idade desempenham um papel vital neste esforço coletivo, devendo a investigação proposta adotar uma abordagem com múltiplos intervenientes.

Neste contexto, a investigação proposta deve explorar os padrões complexos e dinâmicos dos comportamentos dos utilizadores na era digital, investigando a forma como os indivíduos procuram, avaliam e interagem com a informação em linha e fora de linha. Essa exploração beneficiará da inclusão de uma análise da dinâmica emocional na divulgação da desinformação e da polarização nas plataformas digitais. Este aspeto é especialmente relevante em contextos de crise em que a manipulação da informação e a desinformação por parte de agentes estrangeiros podem ser aproveitadas para aumentar o pânico e a confusão. As propostas devem investigar a forma como os algoritmos amplificam os conteúdos emotivos, promovendo a polarização e minando a confiança nas instituições democráticas, bem como a resposta a situações de crise, e desenvolver estratégias de literacia digital e mediática para combater narrativas emocionalmente manipuladoras, como os discursos populistas e pós-verdade.

A investigação deve também examinar os fatores que influenciam a literacia digital, os hábitos de procura de informação e a participação em linha, com destaque para a melhoria da participação e do envolvimento dos cidadãos através de meios digitais (incluindo através da tecnologia cívica) e da tomada de decisões informadas. Numa altura em que a desinformação é utilizada para semear discórdia explorando os receios dos cidadãos, é fundamental assegurar que as decisões democráticas sejam informadas pelos factos e fontes de informação mais fiáveis e amplamente aceites disponíveis. A investigação deve explorar o papel fundamental que a literacia digital e mediática pode desempenhar na promoção da resiliência societal e da integridade da informação, permitindo aos cidadãos navegar e resistir à desinformação e à desinformação.

As propostas devem planear uma avaliação crítica das iniciativas de literacia mediática e digital [6], a fim de avaliar se os esforços existentes estão a reforçar a resiliência dos cidadãos ou se são necessárias novas abordagens para equipar mais eficazmente os cidadãos contra a evolução das táticas de manipulação.

A investigação deve identificar estratégias para melhorar a literacia mediática e a literacia digital e mediática, a fim de reforçar o pensamento crítico, promover a tomada de decisões com base em dados concretos e combater os impactos negativos da desinformação nas sociedades democráticas. A fim de facilitar a geração de soluções práticas para educadores e decisores políticos, a investigação poderá utilizar ferramentas computacionais, como a análise das redes sociais e o tratamento das línguas naturais, para cartografar e atenuar a disseminação da desinformação em várias plataformas. Tal inclui a identificação do Comportamento Coordenado Intangível e a análise de conteúdos textuais e visuais para fundamentar iniciativas de literacia mediática.

As propostas são incentivadas a identificar outros projetos pertinentes financiados pela UE relacionados com a literacia mediática e digital e a explorar potenciais oportunidades de colaboração com os mesmos. Incentiva-se vivamente a agregação e a cooperação com outros projetos selecionados no âmbito deste tópico e com outros projetos pertinentes.

Os projetos selecionados para financiamento são incentivados a colaborar com o JRC para procurar sinergias com o seu trabalho em matéria de inovação para a democracia e a governação pública.

[1] https://commission.europa.eu/topics/defence/safer-together-path-towards-full-prepared-union_en (não traduzido para português).

[2] https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/pt/ip_20_2250

[3] https://commission.europa.eu/strategy-and-policy/priorities-2019-2024/europe-fit-digital-age/digital-services-act_en

[4] https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/european-digital-media-observatory

[5] Comunicação conjunta ao Parlamento Europeu, ao Conselho Europeu, ao Conselho, ao Comité Económico e Social Europeu e ao Comité das Regiões sobre a Estratégia da União Europeia de Preparação

[6] Por exemplo, «Guidelines for teachers and educators on tackling disinformation and promoting digital literacy through education and training» [Orientações para professores e educadores sobre o combate à desinformação e a promoção da literacia digital através da educação e da formação], Serviço das Publicações da União Europeia, 2022, https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2766/28248; ou as «Global Standards for Media and Information Literacy Curricula Development Guidelines» da UNESCO.

O Manual em linha é o seu guia sobre os procedimentos, desde a apresentação de propostas até à gestão da sua subvenção.

O Guia do Programa Horizonte Europa contém orientações pormenorizadas sobre a estrutura, o orçamento e as prioridades políticas do Horizonte Europa.

Perguntas frequentes sobre o portal Funding & Tenders – encontrar as respostas às perguntas mais frequentes sobre a apresentação de propostas, a avaliação e a gestão das subvenções.

Serviço de Consulta sobre Investigação – colocar questões sobre qualquer aspeto da investigação europeia em geral e dos Programas-Quadro de Investigação da UE em particular.

Pontos de Contacto Nacionais (PCN) – obter orientações, informações práticas e assistência sobre a participação no Horizonte Europa. Existem também PCN em muitos países terceiros e não associados («países terceiros»).

Rede Europeia de Empresas – contacte o seu contacto nacional da REE para aconselhamento às empresas, com especial destaque para as PME. O apoio inclui orientações sobre o financiamento da investigação da UE.

Serviço de assistência informática – contactar o serviço de assistência informática do portal Funding & Tenders para questões como palavras-passe esquecidas, direitos e funções de acesso, aspetos técnicos da apresentação de propostas, etc.

O Serviço Europeu de Assistência em matéria de DPI presta-lhe assistência em questões de propriedade intelectual.

CEN-CENELEC Research Helpdesk e ETSI Research Helpdesk – as organizações europeias de normalização aconselham-no sobre a forma de abordar a normalização na sua proposta de projeto.

A Carta Europeia do Investigador e o Código de Conduta para o seu recrutamento – consultar os princípios e requisitos gerais que especificam as funções, responsabilidades e direitos dos investigadores, empregadores e financiadores de investigadores.

A Pesquisa de Parceiros ajuda-o a encontrar uma organização parceira para a sua proposta.

title: Facilitate the engagement of European stakeholders in international digital standardisation (CSA)
destinationDetails:
Through the European Partnership on Virtual Worlds, Europe will drive investment in advanced hardware, immersive interaction, and seamless integration across the Telco-Cloud-to-Edge continuum, enabling lifelike multisensory experiences and fully interoperable platforms. These efforts will enhance Europe’s capacity to innovate, deploy, and scale trustworthy virtual worlds, thereby strengthening competitiveness, resilience, and alignment with EU values.At the same time, a robust Web 4.0 architectural framework — underpinned by open-source solutions and shared standards — will be essential to ensure interoperability, decentralisation, and trust. By deepening Europe’s engagement in international digital standardisation, the Union will help shape global norms in line with its strategic interests, technological sovereignty, and core values.

Legal entities established in China are not eligible to participate in both Research and Innovation Actions (RIAs) and Innovation Actions (IAs) falling under this destination. For additional information please see “Restrictions on the participation of legal entities established in China” found in General Annex B of the General Annexes.
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

Proposals are expected to contribute to the following outcomes:

  • Increasing the participation and influence of European experts in digital standardisation to promote EU values and strategic interests, contributing to strengthen EU competitiveness in the digital field.
  • Improvement of the skills of European experts, especially from SMEs, R&I institutions, Open-Source community, academia and societal stakeholders, to successfully contribute and lead in the development of digital standards.
  • Development and update of standardisation landscapes and gap analyses of key digital technologies as outlined in the Rolling Plan for ICT Standardisation.
  • Provision of foresight analyses regarding standardisation in new emerging technologies to identify short and medium-term digital standardisation needs to support EU policies and anticipate appropriate participation by EU stakeholders.
  • More awareness of the benefits and competitive advantages of standardisation, in particular for SMEs and researchers, and more visibility of the European digital standardisation ecosystem.

Scope:

Contribute to the implementation of the EU Standardisation Strategy and other policy initiatives such as Europe’s Digital Decade, Apply AI Strategy or the Competitiveness Compass, with an emphasis on supporting the EU’s leading position in global standards-setting of key digital technologies.

The goals are inter alia to 1) strengthen the EU competitiveness in the digital domain; 2) contribute to EU tech sovereignty and 3) promote EU values and interests internationally, by empowering and financially supporting the active participation of European stakeholders in the development of digital international standards.

The objective is to reinforce the presence of experts from the EU and associated Horizon Europe countries in global digital standards setting, especially those coming from SMEs, R&I institutions, Open-Source community, academia and societal stakeholders.

To achieve this objective, proposals under this topic should provide for:

  • Setting up of a management facility to support contributions and leadership (e.g. chairing of technical committees, convenor positions) of European specialists in activities in relation to global digital standardisation
  • When relevant, support financially the hosting of international standardisation meetings (e.g. 3GPP, ISO/IEC JTC1) and workshops in Europe to ease the participation of European experts
  • Landscape and gap analysis of standardisation activities in key digital priority areas, as outlined in the Annual Union Work Programme and the Rolling Plan for ICT standardisation, including identification of new emerging technology areas.
  • Promotion of the relevance and benefits of digital standardisation, especially for strengthening the competitiveness of EU industry, driving sustainability, achieving tech sovereignty, and promoting EU values. The proposal shall build synergies with other similar EU- and national-funded initiatives. It shall also include actions, including development of tools and materials, to promote education and skills on standardisation.

Beneficiaries that intend to transfer ownership or grant an exclusive licence must formally notify the granting authority (i.e. DG-CNECT and HaDEA) before the intended transfer or licensing takes place and the granting authority may up to four years after the end of the action object to a transfer of ownership or the exclusive licensing of results.

The proposal should take into account the previous activities carried out at least in terms of educational material and facilities for funding experts within the topics ICT-40-2017 (implemented by the StandICT.eu project), ICT-45-2020 (implemented under StandICT.eu2023 project), HORIZON-CL4-2022-RESILIENCE-01-21 (implemented under StandICT.eu 2026) and HORIZON-CL4-2024-HUMAN-03-04 (implemented under StandICT.eu 2029).

See website: http://www.standict.eu.

Online Manual is your guide on the procedures from proposal submission to managing your grant.

Horizon Europe Programme Guide contains the detailed guidance to the structure, budget and political priorities of Horizon Europe.

Funding & Tenders Portal FAQ – find the answers to most frequently asked questions on submission of proposals, evaluation and grant management.

Research Enquiry Service – ask questions about any aspect of European research in general and the EU Research Framework Programmes in particular.

National Contact Points (NCPs) – get guidance, practical information and assistance on participation in Horizon Europe. There are also NCPs in many non-EU and non-associated countries (‘third-countries’).

Enterprise Europe Network – contact your EEN national contact for advice to businesses with special focus on SMEs. The support includes guidance on the EU research funding.

IT Helpdesk – contact the Funding & Tenders Portal IT helpdesk for questions such as forgotten passwords, access rights and roles, technical aspects of submission of proposals, etc.

European IPR Helpdesk assists you on intellectual property issues.

CEN-CENELEC Research Helpdesk and ETSI Research Helpdesk – the European Standards Organisations advise you how to tackle standardisation in your project proposal.

The European Charter for Researchers and the Code of Conduct for their recruitment – consult the general principles and requirements specifying the roles, responsibilities and entitlements of researchers, employers and funders of researchers.

Partner Search help you find a partner organisation for your proposal.

For additional information please see “Restrictions on the participation of legal entities established in China” found in General Annex B of the General Annexes.
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

Proposals are expected to contribute to the following outcomes:

  • Increasing the participation and influence of European experts in digital standardisation to promote EU values and strategic interests, contributing to strengthen EU competitiveness in the digital field.
  • Improvement of the skills of European experts, especially from SMEs, R&I institutions, Open-Source community, academia and societal stakeholders, to successfully contribute and lead in the development of digital standards.
  • Development and update of standardisation landscapes and gap analyses of key digital technologies as outlined in the Rolling Plan for ICT Standardisation.
  • Provision of foresight analyses regarding standardisation in new emerging technologies to identify short and medium-term digital standardisation needs to support EU policies and anticipate appropriate participation by EU stakeholders.
  • More awareness of the benefits and competitive advantages of standardisation, in particular for SMEs and researchers, and more visibility of the European digital standardisation ecosystem.

Scope:

Contribute to the implementation of the EU Standardisation Strategy and other policy initiatives such as Europe’s Digital Decade, Apply AI Strategy or the Competitiveness Compass, with an emphasis on supporting the EU’s leading position in global standards-setting of key digital technologies.

The goals are inter alia to 1) strengthen the EU competitiveness in the digital domain; 2) contribute to EU tech sovereignty and 3) promote EU values and interests internationally, by empowering and financially supporting the active participation of European stakeholders in the development of digital international standards.

The objective is to reinforce the presence of experts from the EU and associated Horizon Europe countries in global digital standards setting, especially those coming from SMEs, R&I institutions, Open-Source community, academia and societal stakeholders.

To achieve this objective, proposals under this topic should provide for:

  • Setting up of a management facility to support contributions and leadership (e.g. chairing of technical committees, convenor positions) of European specialists in activities in relation to global digital standardisation
  • When relevant, support financially the hosting of international standardisation meetings (e.g. 3GPP, ISO/IEC JTC1) and workshops in Europe to ease the participation of European experts
  • Landscape and gap analysis of standardisation activities in key digital priority areas, as outlined in the Annual Union Work Programme and the Rolling Plan for ICT standardisation, including identification of new emerging technology areas.
  • Promotion of the relevance and benefits of digital standardisation, especially for strengthening the competitiveness of EU industry, driving sustainability, achieving tech sovereignty, and promoting EU values. The proposal shall build synergies with other similar EU- and national-funded initiatives. It shall also include actions, including development of tools and materials, to promote education and skills on standardisation.

Beneficiaries that intend to transfer ownership or grant an exclusive licence must formally notify the granting authority (i.e. DG-CNECT and HaDEA) before the intended transfer or licensing takes place and the granting authority may up to four years after the end of the action object to a transfer of ownership or the exclusive licensing of results.

The proposal should take into account the previous activities carried out at least in terms of educational material and facilities for funding experts within the topics ICT-40-2017 (implemented by the StandICT.eu project), ICT-45-2020 (implemented under StandICT.eu2023 project), HORIZON-CL4-2022-RESILIENCE-01-21 (implemented under StandICT.eu 2026) and HORIZON-CL4-2024-HUMAN-03-04 (implemented under StandICT.eu 2029).

See website: http://www.standict.eu.

title: Secure PQC implementations, Cryptanalysis and Post-quantum Digital Trust
callTitle: Indirectly Managed Action by the ECCC (2027)
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

Proposals are expected to contribute one or more of the following:

  • Practical robust implementations of PQC schemes that can withstand implementation attacks including side-channel attacks, fault attacks and combined attacks, and design of automated tools for evaluating the security of PQC implementations. Comprehensive guidelines for implementing countermeasures against a wide range of attacks;
  • Advances in understanding the quantum hardness of mathematical problem classes; new quantum algorithms and improvements in quantum programming and implementation; security validation methods; design of post-quantum schemes with improved security against quantum and AI-based attacks;
  • Post-quantum schemes and protocols to support privacy-friendly applications and services, ncluding the secure and private use of electronic identities. Design of new digital signatures, key encapsulation mechanisms, and other schemes or use of existing ones to build new verification protocols.

Scope:

Securing PQC algorithm implementations is vital to protect against implementation attacks, such as side channel attacks, fault attacks and combinations of these, which may be amplified by deep learning. Current countermeasures incur significant overhead, and new approaches are needed to balance security and performance. Formal verification tools and methodologies can help achieve this goal and provide machine-readable evidence. Furthermore, to boost confidence in PQC systems, their security should be assessed, including the potential impact of new quantum algorithms or new optimizations of existing ones, also combined with AI.

Another key research area is digital trust in the post-quantum era, which requires transforming various areas, such as secure identities, data protection, access to essential services, and applications such as backup recovery, browser extensions and others into trusted and reliable solutions, via new post-quantum schemes and advanced building blocks for privacy-enhancing protocols.

Proposals should address one of the following technology areas:

  • Development of solutions to prevent implementation attacks, balancing security, performance and cost; research in new attacks, including AI-powered ones, and/or combination of attacks, to inform secure design; creation of testing frameworks for automated security evaluations; improvement of formal verification methodologies.
  • Quantum hardness analysis, via the study of the impact of new quantum algorithms or improvement of existing quantum algorithm implementations as well as the impact of AI-supported quantum attacks; analysis of cryptanalysis results; design of new post-quantum schemes using the information of the advances achieved/ fine-tuning of parameters sets.
  • Design of quantum-resistant schemes and protocols supporting the field of privacy-friendly applications and services, including electronic identities, verification protocols and pseudonymous access options, protocols for attestation and anonymous attestation, for real world scenarios, via the design of new digital signature schemes and key encapsulation mechanisms, design of advanced cryptographic schemes, and usage of existing schemes in new protocols, for post-quantum digital identity and digital trust systems.

destinationDetails:
Leadership in frontier technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Quantum, Photonics and Semiconductors is essential to Europe’s economic security and global competitiveness. Building on the ambition of becoming the “AI Continent” and in line with the concrete actions devised in the Apply AI Strategy[1], the EU will consolidate its world-class research ecosystem through initiatives like the RAISE network of AI science labs, the development of safe and efficient frontier AI models, and the deployment of next-generation AI agents and robotics in strategic sectors. In parallel, a long-term quantum strategy will reinforce Europe’s excellence across quantum computing, sensing and communication, supported by new infrastructures and standardisation to secure technological sovereignty. Photonics and semiconductor technologies will remain critical enablers for the digital and green transitions, with investments in advanced integrated photonic devices and resilient semiconductor ecosystems ensuring Europe’s capacity to innovate, scale and compete globally. Foresight and support to emerging materials and technologies will further strengthen Europe’s position at the cutting edge to make sure Europe’s does not miss the emergence of new disruptive technologies, aligning with the Draghi report and the Competitiveness Compass to secure a cohesive, sovereign and future-proof European industrial base.

Legal entities established in China are not eligible to participate in both Research and Innovation Actions (RIAs) and Innovation Actions (IAs) falling under this destination. For additional information please see “Restrictions on the participation of legal entities established in China” found in General Annex B of the General Annexes.

[1] COM(2025)723 Apply AI Strategy
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

  • European leadership in foresight activities on future enabling technologies and their transformational potential in industrial, societal and environmental terms.
  • Increased collaboration between academia, industry players and other relevant stakeholders in iterative and multidisciplinary approaches for co-creating the enabling technologies of the future.
  • Alignment with national or regional initiatives creating an expanding innovation ecosystem, anchored in local contexts across Europe, for selected emerging technologies.
  • Accelerating the pick-up of novel advanced technology by industry and society.

Scope:

Proposals should establish a forum for emerging interdisciplinary areas and new technological visions.

Proposals should enable and support a broad range of participants (across disciplines in science and engineering, RTOs, industry sectors, stakeholders) to meet, mutually inspire, cooperate and develop together innovative ideas for future enabling digital technologies covering from fundamental research up to proof of concept.

Proposals should involve and be driven by representatives of the relevant actors of the field (e.g., academia, RTOs, industry including SMEs).

Proposals should consider civil society engagement for seeking wider input.

Proposals should connect with analogous EC-internal activities, either ongoing (e.g. FOSI4EIC involving EISMEA and JRC) or foreseen, such as the Competitiveness Coordination Tool and the technology observatory envisaged in the FP10 regulation.

Beneficiaries that intend to transfer ownership or grant an exclusive licence must formally notify the granting authority (i.e. DG-CNECT and HaDEA) before the intended transfer or licensing takes place and the granting authority may up to four years after the end of the action object to a transfer of ownership or the exclusive licensing of results.

title: Societal resilience, engagement of the younger generations and digital innovation for disaster resilience
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

Project results are expected to contribute to some or all of the following expected outcomes:

  • Developed a tailored education programs for younger generations, incorporating digital tools and gamification to enhance disaster awareness and engagement;
  • Strengthened societal resilience by actively involving younger generations, citizens, and local authorities in disaster preparedness and response initiatives;
  • Promoted collaborative research that integrates youth perspectives and community involvement, fostering a more resilient society in the face of disasters and crises;
  • Enhanced resilience and behaviour of children, young people, and other groups in a vulnerable situation before, during, and after climate-related disasters and health emergencies;
  • Training and education tools to engage young people and other populations a vulnerable situation in preparedness and crisis management.

Scope:

This topic focuses on enhancing societal resilience by actively engaging younger generations in disaster preparedness, response, and recovery through digital innovation, education, and community involvement. Projects should develop tailored innovative solutions that integrate digital tools, gamification, and interactive learning methods to improve disaster awareness, risk perception, and response capabilities among younger generations. These initiatives should empower younger generations[1], to become active contributors to resilience-building efforts, equipping them with the knowledge and leadership skills.

Particular attention should be given to the behaviour of children, young people, and other groups in a vulnerable situation before, during, and after climate-related disasters and health emergencies. Participatory approaches, including youth-led initiatives, citizen science, and digital engagement platforms, should be prioritized to enhance community-based resilience and ensure young people’s perspectives are integrated into decision-making processes. These approaches should follow an intersectional approach that gives credit to the (growing) heterogeneity of young people. Best practices from other programmes should be taken into account.

Proposals should also focus on leveraging emerging technologies - such as artificial intelligence, virtual and augmented reality, social media analytics, and serious games - to engage young people in disaster preparedness and crisis response. Additionally, innovative communication strategies should be explored to enhance youth participation, particularly through digital technologies and social media. Practical examples, including pilots and real-world case studies, should be developed to test and refine these approaches.

Proposals should explore methods to interconnect young people’s data with crisis management teams, practitioners, and authorities, ensuring that their contributions are effectively integrated into emergency response frameworks. Training and education tools should be designed to engage young people and other vulnerable populations in preparedness and crisis management, promoting long-term resilience.

Projects should conduct a stakeholder or market analysis and a roadmap or plan for uptake of the developed methodologies, findings, and technologies to the industry, the research and innovation community, and/or the relevant authorities.

The support and involvement of citizens and civil society is central to achieving the targeted outcomes.

By fostering collaborative research and youth-driven initiatives, projects should contribute to innovative and inclusive resilience strategies that align with EU policies on disaster risk reduction, education, digital transformation, and civil protection. Proposals should ensure synergies with existing initiatives and frameworks, such as the Preparedness Union Strategy’s chapter on population preparedness, Erasmus+ and the European Solidarity Corps, as well as the Sendai Disaster Risk Reduction Framework. Finding synergies with projects from operational grants, such as the Knowledge for Action in Prevention & Preparedness (KAPP)[2], is recommend.

null

Activities are expected to achieve TRL 5 by the end of the project – see General Annex B.

[1] In the context of the European Union, youth is typically defined as individuals between the ages of 13 and 30. This definition aligns with the EU's Youth Strategy, which focuses on supporting young people’s personal and professional development. However, some EU programs may adjust the age range slightly depending on the specific context (e.g., education, employment, or participation), but the 13-30 age bracket is recognized in EU policies related to youth.

[2] Knowledge for Action in Prevention and Preparedness (KAPP) - European Commission - https://civil-protection-humanitarian-aid.ec.europa.eu/funding-evaluations/financing-civil-protection/cp-calls-proposals/knowledge-action-prevention-and-preparedness-kapp-0_en

descriptionByte:
Resultado esperado:

  • Otimização do quadro operacional de D&E para o Programa Europa Digital, tendo em conta os elementos mencionados no âmbito de aplicação, com abordagens metodológicas e práticas sólidas.
  • Identificação de diferentes tipos de adotantes e criação de uma taxonomia que articule os respetivos interesses e necessidades.
  • Apoio a projetos na preparação e execução de atividades de D&E, incluindo a valorização e a adoção dos resultados através de serviços de aconselhamento, apoio às empresas e aceleração
  • Um plano para concretizar o quadro operacional apoiado por métricas de acompanhamento e avaliação.
  • A realização de ações de execução do quadro operacional e a participação das partes interessadas, se for caso disso, incluindo eventos setoriais e a nível do programa.
  • Os meios e instrumentos para facilitar a execução do quadro operacional, incluindo os requisitos funcionais e técnicos para uma plataforma de resultados específica.
  • Um plano para a sustentabilidade do quadro operacional e das ações executadas pelo projeto.
  • Difusão e exploração dos resultados (incluindo o acesso às infraestruturas) no contexto específico das restrições de segurança e da proteção dos interesses da UE em geral.
  • Produzir uma base de dados com casos concretos de resultados do PED, em todos os objetivos específicos e organismos de execução, com divulgação e utilização exemplares dos resultados.

Objectivo:

Maximizar o impacto do Programa Europa Digital e a adoção dos seus resultados através de um quadro operacional de divulgação e exploração (D&E) e da execução de ações práticas apoiadas por instrumentos adequados. A ação impulsionará os esforços de D&E já em curso a nível do programa e reforçá-los-á.

O Programa Europa Digital procura melhorar a valorização dos resultados dos projetos e a sua adoção efetiva. Espera-se, por conseguinte, que as atividades de divulgação e exploração (D&E) contribuam substancialmente para a realização dos objetivos do programa.

As ações financiadas pelo programa devem executar atividades de difusão e exploração eficientes e direcionadas, a fim de aumentar o impacto do financiamento da UE. Para além dos trabalhos D&E de projetos individuais, o programa financia atividades de apoio em determinados domínios temáticos que apoiam os projetos na respetiva área.

Além disso, existe uma clara necessidade de uma perspetiva global do programa em matéria de D&E. Uma ação de coordenação e apoio em curso (DEDEP.eu) está a conceber um quadro conceptual e operacional para a execução de atividades eficazes de D&E no programa, ajudando os projetos financiados a partilhar estrategicamente os resultados com as partes interessadas pertinentes e a criar um corpus de materiais e ferramentas reutilizáveis.

O programa está agora a entrar numa fase crucial em que muitas iniciativas estão a produzir resultados tangíveis. Colocar uma forte ênfase na divulgação e exploração destes resultados assegurará uma maior aceitação dos resultados existentes e futuros e amplificará significativamente o impacto global do programa.

Âmbito de aplicação:

A ação abordará, pelo menos, as seguintes dimensões:

  • O programa global, os seus Objetivos Específicos (OE) e as respetivas áreas, até tópicos e projetos, se for caso disso, em todos os instrumentos de financiamento, em especial subvenções, contratos públicos e instrumentos financeiros;
  • As vertentes de reforço das capacidades e utilização do Programa Europa Digital, tendo em conta o tipo de resultados e o seu público de divulgação e exploração;
  • Os diferentes tipos de organizações que participam no programa;
  • As diferentes partes interessadas, incluindo os utilizadores finais e/ou os utilizadores dos resultados;
  • As fases do ciclo de vida do projeto e as obrigações de comunicação de informações;
  • As especificidades de segurança e autonomia estratégica do programa, incluindo as implicações na utilização de infraestruturas críticas e na exploração dos resultados;
  • coordenação dentro e fora da UE, se for caso disso, tendo em conta as prioridades e iniciativas políticas;
    • no âmbito do próprio Programa Europa Digital, identificar e explorar complementaridades de projetos entre OE e temas, incluindo ações específicas de coordenação e apoio a OE e agregadores de projetos;
    • entre o Programa Europa Digital, outros programas da UE e programas nacionais/regionais;
    • dos diferentes organismos de execução do programa, por exemplo, a Comissão Europeia, a Agência de Execução para a Saúde e o Digital (HADEA), as empresas comuns (EC) e organismos semelhantes, tendo em conta as suas especificidades no tratamento dos resultados resultantes das suas ações. A ação complementará e enriquecerá as atividades de D&E dos projetos do programa. A ação proporcionará meios que podem ajudar a alcançar o seu objetivo, incluindo a mobilização de instrumentos já existentes, por exemplo de outros programas da UE, e a utilização de abordagens inovadoras em matéria de D&E. A ação promoverá a adoção dos resultados do Programa Europa Digital para além das entidades diretamente envolvidas nos projetos do programa.

title: Horizon scanning and foresight in future enabling digital technologies (CSA)
destinationDetails:
Leadership in frontier technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Quantum, Photonics and Semiconductors is essential to Europe’s economic security and global competitiveness. Building on the ambition of becoming the “AI Continent” and in line with the concrete actions devised in the Apply AI Strategy[1], the EU will consolidate its world-class research ecosystem through initiatives like the RAISE network of AI science labs, the development of safe and efficient frontier AI models, and the deployment of next-generation AI agents and robotics in strategic sectors. In parallel, a long-term quantum strategy will reinforce Europe’s excellence across quantum computing, sensing and communication, supported by new infrastructures and standardisation to secure technological sovereignty. Photonics and semiconductor technologies will remain critical enablers for the digital and green transitions, with investments in advanced integrated photonic devices and resilient semiconductor ecosystems ensuring Europe’s capacity to innovate, scale and compete globally. Foresight and support to emerging materials and technologies will further strengthen Europe’s position at the cutting edge to make sure Europe’s does not miss the emergence of new disruptive technologies, aligning with the Draghi report and the Competitiveness Compass to secure a cohesive, sovereign and future-proof European industrial base.

Legal entities established in China are not eligible to participate in both Research and Innovation Actions (RIAs) and Innovation Actions (IAs) falling under this destination. For additional information please see “Restrictions on the participation of legal entities established in China” found in General Annex B of the General Annexes.

[1] COM(2025)723 Apply AI Strategy
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

  • European leadership in foresight activities on future enabling technologies and their transformational potential in industrial, societal and environmental terms.
  • Increased collaboration between academia, industry players and other relevant stakeholders in iterative and multidisciplinary approaches for co-creating the enabling technologies of the future.
  • Alignment with national or regional initiatives creating an expanding innovation ecosystem, anchored in local contexts across Europe, for selected emerging technologies.
  • Accelerating the pick-up of novel advanced technology by industry and society.

Scope:

Proposals should establish a forum for emerging interdisciplinary areas and new technological visions.

Proposals should enable and support a broad range of participants (across disciplines in science and engineering, RTOs, industry sectors, stakeholders) to meet, mutually inspire, cooperate and develop together innovative ideas for future enabling digital technologies covering from fundamental research up to proof of concept.

Proposals should involve and be driven by representatives of the relevant actors of the field (e.g., academia, RTOs, industry including SMEs).

Proposals should consider civil society engagement for seeking wider input.

Proposals should connect with analogous EC-internal activities, either ongoing (e.g. FOSI4EIC involving EISMEA and JRC) or foreseen, such as the Competitiveness Coordination Tool and the technology observatory envisaged in the FP10 regulation.

Beneficiaries that intend to transfer ownership or grant an exclusive licence must formally notify the granting authority (i.e. DG-CNECT and HaDEA) before the intended transfer or licensing takes place and the granting authority may up to four years after the end of the action object to a transfer of ownership or the exclusive licensing of results.

Online Manual is your guide on the procedures from proposal submission to managing your grant.

Horizon Europe Programme Guide contains the detailed guidance to the structure, budget and political priorities of Horizon Europe.

Funding & Tenders Portal FAQ – find the answers to most frequently asked questions on submission of proposals, evaluation and grant management.

Research Enquiry Service – ask questions about any aspect of European research in general and the EU Research Framework Programmes in particular.

National Contact Points (NCPs) – get guidance, practical information and assistance on participation in Horizon Europe. There are also NCPs in many non-EU and non-associated countries (‘third-countries’).

Enterprise Europe Network – contact your EEN national contact for advice to businesses with special focus on SMEs. The support includes guidance on the EU research funding.

IT Helpdesk – contact the Funding & Tenders Portal IT helpdesk for questions such as forgotten passwords, access rights and roles, technical aspects of submission of proposals, etc.

European IPR Helpdesk assists you on intellectual property issues.

CEN-CENELEC Research Helpdesk and ETSI Research Helpdesk – the European Standards Organisations advise you how to tackle standardisation in your project proposal.

The European Charter for Researchers and the Code of Conduct for their recruitment – consult the general principles and requirements specifying the roles, responsibilities and entitlements of researchers, employers and funders of researchers.

Partner Search help you find a partner organisation for your proposal.

title: Horizon scanning and foresight in future enabling digital technologies (CSA)
destinationDetails:
Leadership in frontier technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Quantum, Photonics and Semiconductors is essential to Europe’s economic security and global competitiveness. Building on the ambition of becoming the “AI Continent” and in line with the concrete actions devised in the Apply AI Strategy[1], the EU will consolidate its world-class research ecosystem through initiatives like the RAISE network of AI science labs, the development of safe and efficient frontier AI models, and the deployment of next-generation AI agents and robotics in strategic sectors. In parallel, a long-term quantum strategy will reinforce Europe’s excellence across quantum computing, sensing and communication, supported by new infrastructures and standardisation to secure technological sovereignty. Photonics and semiconductor technologies will remain critical enablers for the digital and green transitions, with investments in advanced integrated photonic devices and resilient semiconductor ecosystems ensuring Europe’s capacity to innovate, scale and compete globally. Foresight and support to emerging materials and technologies will further strengthen Europe’s position at the cutting edge to make sure Europe’s does not miss the emergence of new disruptive technologies, aligning with the Draghi report and the Competitiveness Compass to secure a cohesive, sovereign and future-proof European industrial base.

Legal entities established in China are not eligible to participate in both Research and Innovation Actions (RIAs) and Innovation Actions (IAs) falling under this destination. For additional information please see “Restrictions on the participation of legal entities established in China” found in General Annex B of the General Annexes.

[1] COM(2025)723 Apply AI Strategy
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

  • European leadership in foresight activities on future enabling technologies and their transformational potential in industrial, societal and environmental terms.
  • Increased collaboration between academia, industry players and other relevant stakeholders in iterative and multidisciplinary approaches for co-creating the enabling technologies of the future.
  • Alignment with national or regional initiatives creating an expanding innovation ecosystem, anchored in local contexts across Europe, for selected emerging technologies.
  • Accelerating the pick-up of novel advanced technology by industry and society.

Scope:

Proposals should establish a forum for emerging interdisciplinary areas and new technological visions.

Proposals should enable and support a broad range of participants (across disciplines in science and engineering, RTOs, industry sectors, stakeholders) to meet, mutually inspire, cooperate and develop together innovative ideas for future enabling digital technologies covering from fundamental research up to proof of concept.

Proposals should involve and be driven by representatives of the relevant actors of the field (e.g., academia, RTOs, industry including SMEs).

Proposals should consider civil society engagement for seeking wider input.

Proposals should connect with analogous EC-internal activities, either ongoing (e.g. FOSI4EIC involving EISMEA and JRC) or foreseen, such as the Competitiveness Coordination Tool and the technology observatory envisaged in the FP10 regulation.

Beneficiaries that intend to transfer ownership or grant an exclusive licence must formally notify the granting authority (i.e. DG-CNECT and HaDEA) before the intended transfer or licensing takes place and the granting authority may up to four years after the end of the action object to a transfer of ownership or the exclusive licensing of results.

title: Facilitate the engagement of European stakeholders in international digital standardisation (CSA)
destinationDetails:
Through the European Partnership on Virtual Worlds, Europe will drive investment in advanced hardware, immersive interaction, and seamless integration across the Telco-Cloud-to-Edge continuum, enabling lifelike multisensory experiences and fully interoperable platforms. These efforts will enhance Europe’s capacity to innovate, deploy, and scale trustworthy virtual worlds, thereby strengthening competitiveness, resilience, and alignment with EU values.At the same time, a robust Web 4.0 architectural framework — underpinned by open-source solutions and shared standards — will be essential to ensure interoperability, decentralisation, and trust. By deepening Europe’s engagement in international digital standardisation, the Union will help shape global norms in line with its strategic interests, technological sovereignty, and core values.

Legal entities established in China are not eligible to participate in both Research and Innovation Actions (RIAs) and Innovation Actions (IAs) falling under this destination. descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

Proposals are expected to contribute to the following outcomes:

  • Increasing the participation and influence of European experts in digital standardisation to promote EU values and strategic interests, contributing to strengthen EU competitiveness in the digital field.
  • Improvement of the skills of European experts, especially from SMEs, R&I institutions, Open-Source community, academia and societal stakeholders, to successfully contribute and lead in the development of digital standards.
  • Development and update of standardisation landscapes and gap analyses of key digital technologies as outlined in the Rolling Plan for ICT Standardisation.
  • Provision of foresight analyses regarding standardisation in new emerging technologies to identify short and medium-term digital standardisation needs to support EU policies and anticipate appropriate participation by EU stakeholders.
  • More awareness of the benefits and competitive advantages of standardisation, in particular for SMEs and researchers, and more visibility of the European digital standardisation ecosystem.

Scope:

Contribute to the implementation of the EU Standardisation Strategy and other policy initiatives such as Europe’s Digital Decade, Apply AI Strategy or the Competitiveness Compass, with an emphasis on supporting the EU’s leading position in global standards-setting of key digital technologies.

The goals are inter alia to 1) strengthen the EU competitiveness in the digital domain; 2) contribute to EU tech sovereignty and 3) promote EU values and interests internationally, by empowering and financially supporting the active participation of European stakeholders in the development of digital international standards.

The objective is to reinforce the presence of experts from the EU and associated Horizon Europe countries in global digital standards setting, especially those coming from SMEs, R&I institutions, Open-Source community, academia and societal stakeholders.

To achieve this objective, proposals under this topic should provide for:

  • Setting up of a management facility to support contributions and leadership (e.g. chairing of technical committees, convenor positions) of European specialists in activities in relation to global digital standardisation
  • When relevant, support financially the hosting of international standardisation meetings (e.g. 3GPP, ISO/IEC JTC1) and workshops in Europe to ease the participation of European experts
  • Landscape and gap analysis of standardisation activities in key digital priority areas, as outlined in the Annual Union Work Programme and the Rolling Plan for ICT standardisation, including identification of new emerging technology areas.
  • Promotion of the relevance and benefits of digital standardisation, especially for strengthening the competitiveness of EU industry, driving sustainability, achieving tech sovereignty, and promoting EU values. The proposal shall build synergies with other similar EU- and national-funded initiatives. It shall also include actions, including development of tools and materials, to promote education and skills on standardisation.

Beneficiaries that intend to transfer ownership or grant an exclusive licence must formally notify the granting authority (i.e. DG-CNECT and HaDEA) before the intended transfer or licensing takes place and the granting authority may up to four years after the end of the action object to a transfer of ownership or the exclusive licensing of results.

The proposal should take into account the previous activities carried out at least in terms of educational material and facilities for funding experts within the topics ICT-40-2017 (implemented by the StandICT.eu project), ICT-45-2020 (implemented under StandICT.eu2023 project), HORIZON-CL4-2022-RESILIENCE-01-21 (implemented under StandICT.eu 2026) and HORIZON-CL4-2024-HUMAN-03-04 (implemented under StandICT.eu 2029).

See website: http://www.standict.eu.

Partner Search help you find a partner organisation for your proposal.

descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

The focus needs to be on areas where Digital Partnership countries bring strong complementary expertise, including advanced packaging, heterogeneous integration, and photonic chip technologies. The topic would aim to foster collaboration between European and Digital Partnership countries’ R&I communities. Projects are expected to contribute to the following outcomes:

• Innovative design and integration concepts for neuromorphic computing systems supporting very low energy consumption, connectivity, embedded functions for mobile applications.

• Alternative manufacturing process technologies for semiconductor chips including frontend or backend for heterogenous integration. The technologies should sustain in the mid- and long-term the fast-paced evolution of device performance, miniaturisation and cost, while reducing the environmental footprint.

• Very advanced packaging solutions aiming heterogeneous integration of multiple functions and materials for applications in communication (RF, mmW or THz), sensing, actuating, power management and active/passive integration.

6. Legal and financial set-up of the grants

The granting authority may, up to 4 years after the end of the action, object to a transfer of ownership or to the exclusive licensing of results, as set out in the specific provision of Annex 5.

Beneficiaries may provide financial support to third parties (FSTP). The support to third parties can only be provided in the form of grants. The maximum amount to be granted to each third party is EUR 60 000. As the primary purpose of the action is to support European experts in the global ICT standardisation scene, a minimum of 75% of the total requested EU contribution should be allocated to FSTP selected through open calls. Beneficiaries will define the process for the selection of specialists through open calls. They will also define the process that will lead to a selection of a pool of evaluators that will evaluate the applications received in the open calls.

Eligible costs will take the form of a lump sum as defined in the Decision of 7 July 2021 authorising the use of lump sum contributions under the Horizon Europe Programme – the Framework Programme for Research and Innovation (2021-2027) – and in actions under the Research and Training Programme of the European Atomic Energy Community (2021-2025) [[This decision is available on the Funding and Tenders Portal, in the reference documents section for Horizon Europe, under ‘Simplified costs decisions’ or through this link: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/docs/2021-2027/horizon/guidance/ls-decision_he_en.pdf]].

title: Facilitate the engagement of European stakeholders in international digital standardisation (CSA)
destinationDetails:
Through the European Partnership on Virtual Worlds, Europe will drive investment in advanced hardware, immersive interaction, and seamless integration across the Telco-Cloud-to-Edge continuum, enabling lifelike multisensory experiences and fully interoperable platforms. These efforts will enhance Europe’s capacity to innovate, deploy, and scale trustworthy virtual worlds, thereby strengthening competitiveness, resilience, and alignment with EU values.At the same time, a robust Web 4.0 architectural framework — underpinned by open-source solutions and shared standards — will be essential to ensure interoperability, decentralisation, and trust. By deepening Europe’s engagement in international digital standardisation, the Union will help shape global norms in line with its strategic interests, technological sovereignty, and core values.

Legal entities established in China are not eligible to participate in both Research and Innovation Actions (RIAs) and Innovation Actions (IAs) falling under this destination. For additional information please see “Restrictions on the participation of legal entities established in China” found in General Annex B of the General Annexes.
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

Proposals are expected to contribute to the following outcomes:

  • Increasing the participation and influence of European experts in digital standardisation to promote EU values and strategic interests, contributing to strengthen EU competitiveness in the digital field.
  • Improvement of the skills of European experts, especially from SMEs, R&I institutions, Open-Source community, academia and societal stakeholders, to successfully contribute and lead in the development of digital standards.
  • Development and update of standardisation landscapes and gap analyses of key digital technologies as outlined in the Rolling Plan for ICT Standardisation.
  • Provision of foresight analyses regarding standardisation in new emerging technologies to identify short and medium-term digital standardisation needs to support EU policies and anticipate appropriate participation by EU stakeholders.
  • More awareness of the benefits and competitive advantages of standardisation, in particular for SMEs and researchers, and more visibility of the European digital standardisation ecosystem.

Scope:

Contribute to the implementation of the EU Standardisation Strategy and other policy initiatives such as Europe’s Digital Decade, Apply AI Strategy or the Competitiveness Compass, with an emphasis on supporting the EU’s leading position in global standards-setting of key digital technologies.

The goals are inter alia to 1) strengthen the EU competitiveness in the digital domain; 2) contribute to EU tech sovereignty and 3) promote EU values and interests internationally, by empowering and financially supporting the active participation of European stakeholders in the development of digital international standards.

The objective is to reinforce the presence of experts from the EU and associated Horizon Europe countries in global digital standards setting, especially those coming from SMEs, R&I institutions, Open-Source community, academia and societal stakeholders.

To achieve this objective, proposals under this topic should provide for:

  • Setting up of a management facility to support contributions and leadership (e.g. chairing of technical committees, convenor positions) of European specialists in activities in relation to global digital standardisation
  • When relevant, support financially the hosting of international standardisation meetings (e.g. 3GPP, ISO/IEC JTC1) and workshops in Europe to ease the participation of European experts
  • Landscape and gap analysis of standardisation activities in key digital priority areas, as outlined in the Annual Union Work Programme and the Rolling Plan for ICT standardisation, including identification of new emerging technology areas.
  • Promotion of the relevance and benefits of digital standardisation, especially for strengthening the competitiveness of EU industry, driving sustainability, achieving tech sovereignty, and promoting EU values. The proposal shall build synergies with other similar EU- and national-funded initiatives. It shall also include actions, including development of tools and materials, to promote education and skills on standardisation.

Beneficiaries that intend to transfer ownership or grant an exclusive licence must formally notify the granting authority (i.e. DG-CNECT and HaDEA) before the intended transfer or licensing takes place and the granting authority may up to four years after the end of the action object to a transfer of ownership or the exclusive licensing of results.

The proposal should take into account the previous activities carried out at least in terms of educational material and facilities for funding experts within the topics ICT-40-2017 (implemented by the StandICT.eu project), ICT-45-2020 (implemented under StandICT.eu2023 project), HORIZON-CL4-2022-RESILIENCE-01-21 (implemented under StandICT.eu 2026) and HORIZON-CL4-2024-HUMAN-03-04 (implemented under StandICT.eu 2029).

See website: http://www.standict.eu.

descriptionByte:
Resultado esperado:

A tónica deve ser colocada nos domínios em que os países da Parceria Digital disponibilizam conhecimentos especializados complementares sólidos, incluindo embalagens avançadas, integração heterogénea e tecnologias de circuitos integrados fotónicos. O tema visa promover a colaboração entre as comunidades de I&I dos países da Parceria Europeia e Digital. Espera-se que os projetos contribuam para os seguintes resultados:

• Conceitos inovadores de conceção e integração para sistemas de computação neuromórfica que suportam um consumo de energia muito baixo, conectividade e funções incorporadas para aplicações móveis.

• Tecnologias de processo de fabrico alternativas para circuitos integrados semicondutores, incluindo frontend ou backend para integração heterogénea. As tecnologias devem sustentar, a médio e longo prazo, a rápida evolução do desempenho, da miniaturização e dos custos dos dispositivos, reduzindo simultaneamente a pegada ambiental.

• Soluções de embalagem muito avançadas que visam a integração heterogénea de múltiplas funções e materiais para aplicações em comunicação (RF, mmW ou THz), deteção, acionamento, gestão de energia e integração ativa/passiva.

O Manual em linha é o seu guia sobre os procedimentos, desde a apresentação de propostas até à gestão da sua subvenção.

O Guia do Programa Horizonte Europa contém orientações pormenorizadas sobre a estrutura, o orçamento e as prioridades políticas do Horizonte Europa.

Perguntas frequentes sobre o portal Funding & Tenders – encontrar as respostas às perguntas mais frequentes sobre a apresentação de propostas, a avaliação e a gestão das subvenções.

Serviço de Consulta sobre Investigação – colocar questões sobre qualquer aspeto da investigação europeia em geral e dos Programas-Quadro de Investigação da UE em particular.

Pontos de Contacto Nacionais (PCN) – obter orientações, informações práticas e assistência sobre a participação no Horizonte Europa. Existem também PCN em muitos países terceiros e não associados («países terceiros»).

Rede Europeia de Empresas – contacte o seu contacto nacional da REE para aconselhamento às empresas, com especial destaque para as PME. O apoio inclui orientações sobre o financiamento da investigação da UE.

Serviço de assistência informática – contactar o serviço de assistência informática do portal Funding & Tenders para questões como palavras-passe esquecidas, direitos e funções de acesso, aspetos técnicos da apresentação de propostas, etc.

O Serviço Europeu de Assistência em matéria de DPI presta-lhe assistência em questões de propriedade intelectual.

1. Tillåtlighetsvillkor: Förslagssidans begränsning och layout

Enligt beskrivningen i bilagorna A och E till arbetsprogrammet för Horisont Europa, allmänna bilagor.

Förslagssidans begränsningar och layout: beskrivs i del B i det ansökningsformulär som finns tillgängligt i inlämningssystemet.
