title: Digitale und Medienkompetenz als Triebkräfte für demokratische und bürgerschaftliche Resilienz
destinationDetails:
Rechtsstaatlichkeit, Achtung der Menschenrechte und Demokratie sind die in Artikel 2 des Vertrags über die Europäische Union verankerten Grundwerte der EU. Diese Werte geben der Union prinzipielle Orientierungen, um den unvermeidlichen geopolitischen wirtschaftlichen, sozialen und demografischen Veränderungen zu begegnen, die zum Zeitpunkt der Ausarbeitung der Verträge nicht vorhersehbar waren. Dazu gehört auch, wie sich der digitale Wandel auf die Gestaltung der Debatte und der politischen Prozesse auswirken würde.

Demokratie ist ebenso kulturelle Praxis wie politisches System. Sie ist eine Schlüsselstärke der europäischen Gesellschaften und trägt dazu bei, die Achtung der Gleichheit, der Rechtsstaatlichkeit, der Grundrechte und der Freiheit zu gewährleisten. Akteure mit antidemokratischen Tendenzen greifen Demokratien und ihre Institutionen an, weil die Demokratie ein Schutz gegen sie ist[[[Der Bericht des V-Dem-Instituts aus dem Jahr 2025 („25 Jahre Autokratisierung – Demokratie getrumpft?“) bestätigt die erschreckenden Anzeichen, Indikatoren und Tendenzen, die in früheren Messjahren erfasst wurden: „Der Trend der „dritten Welle der Autokratisierung“ vertieft sich und breitet sich aus. Dazu gehören die Schwächung der Demokratie in einigen etablierten liberalen Demokratien, der Zusammenbruch der Demokratie in Ländern, die den größten Teil des 21. Jahrhunderts demokratisch waren, sowie die Vertiefung der Autokratie in bereits autokratischen Staaten […] Der weltweite demokratische Niedergang vertieft sich, unabhängig davon, wie wir die Daten schneiden und welches Maß wir verwenden“ (S. 9 und 10)]. Selbst traditionell gut funktionierende Demokratien stehen vor vielen Herausforderungen, was bedeutet, dass sie sich auch ständig anpassen müssen, wenn sich die Bedingungen ändern. Die sozial- und geisteswissenschaftliche Forschung (SSH) spielt eine entscheidende Rolle, um aktuelle Herausforderungen und Bedrohungen zu verstehen und zukünftige Wege für innovative Lösungen abzubilden. Aufbauend auf historischen, kulturellen, sozialen, rechtlichen und philosophischen Perspektiven wird die Forschung die Weiterentwicklung der Demokratie fördern, um die Bürgerbeteiligung und die inklusive Politikgestaltung zu verbessern, Gleichheit und Inklusivität zu fördern und die Auswirkungen von KI und den digitalen Wandel der Demokratie anzugehen. Sie wird auch die demokratische Resilienz und die staatsbürgerliche Vorsorge stärken und unter anderem die Rolle freier, unabhängiger und pluralistischer Medien als zentrale Grundsätze der Demokratie wahren.

Erwartete Auswirkungen:

In den Vorschlägen für Themen im Rahmen dieses Ziels sollte ein glaubwürdiger Weg aufgezeigt werden, um zu den folgenden erwarteten Auswirkungen des Strategieplans von Horizont Europa beizutragen:

  • Stärkung der demokratischen Staatsführung durch Verbesserung der Unabhängigkeit, Rechenschaftspflicht, Transparenz, Wirksamkeit und Vertrauenswürdigkeit von Institutionen und politischen Maßnahmen auf der Grundlage der Rechtsstaatlichkeit und durch Ausweitung der aktiven und inklusiven Beteiligung und des Engagements der Bürger, die durch den Schutz der Grundrechte gestärkt werden.

Ziel der Forschungsinvestitionen zur Unterstützung dieser Auswirkungen ist es, eine solide Evidenzbasis zu entwickeln, die in die Festlegung wirksamer, relevanter und vernünftiger Strategien einfließen kann, die die Widerstandsfähigkeit demokratischer Systeme stärken und sie vor Bedrohungen schützen. Gleichzeitig zielt sie darauf ab, kritisches Denken zu fördern und gleichzeitig das Vertrauen der Bürger in die Demokratie, ihre Institutionen und das Gefühl der politischen Teilhabe im weitesten Sinne zu stärken.

Das Ziel strebt Synergien mit anderen einschlägigen EU-Programmen an, insbesondere im Hinblick auf die Übernahme von Forschungsergebnissen und innovativen Lösungen, die im Rahmen von Horizont Europa entwickelt wurden. Die Interaktion – unter anderem – mit folgenden Programmen wird gefördert: Digitales Europa (DIGITAL), Instrument für technische Unterstützung, CERV (Bürger, Gleichstellung, Rechte und Werte), Erasmus+, ESF+ und Europa in der Welt: Instrument für Nachbarschaft, Entwicklungszusammenarbeit und internationale Zusammenarbeit.

Die Antragsteller werden aufgefordert, gegebenenfalls die Dienstleistungen zu berücksichtigen, die von den derzeitigen und künftigen EU-finanzierten europäischen Forschungsinfrastrukturen angeboten werden, insbesondere im Bereich der Sozial- und Geisteswissenschaften [1]. Gegebenenfalls sollten die Vorschläge die Daten und Dienste nutzen, die über europäische Forschungsinfrastrukturen, die im Rahmen der Europäischen Cloud für offene Wissenschaft zusammengeschlossen sind, verfügbar sind, sowie Daten aus einschlägigen Datenräumen.

Da das Ziel direkt auf das Engagement der Bürger und die Schaffung dauerhafter Veränderungen abzielt, ist es von besonderer Bedeutung, dass die Forschungs- und Innovationsmaßnahmen die höchsten Standards für Transparenz und Offenheit fördern. Besondere Anstrengungen sollten unternommen werden, um sicherzustellen, dass die im Zusammenhang mit diesem Ziel erzeugten Daten FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Re-usable) sind. Gegebenenfalls wird empfohlen, den Prozess, die Kriterien, die Methoden und die Daten im Laufe der Forschung der Zivilgesellschaft zugänglich zu machen.

Um die Auswirkungen von FuEmpfehlungen im Rahmen dieses Ziels im Einklang mit den Prioritäten der EU zu maximieren, wird die internationale Zusammenarbeit gefördert, wann immer dies für die vorgeschlagenen Themen relevant ist.

[1] Eine vollständige Liste finden Sie unter https://ri-portfolio.esfri.eu/ri-portfolio/table. Im Bereich der Sozialwissenschaften siehe beispielsweise: CESSDA – Consortium of European Social Science Data Archives (https://www.cessda.eu/), ESS – European Social Survey (https://www.europeansocialsurvey.org/), SHARE – Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (https://www.share-eric.eu/) oder die Europäische Holocaust-Forschungsinfrastruktur (https://ehri-project.eu/)

descriptionByte:
Erwartetes Ergebnis:

Die Projekte sollten zu allen folgenden erwarteten Ergebnissen beitragen:

  • Die EU-Institutionen und die nationalen Entscheidungsträger haben ein besseres Verständnis dafür, wie die demokratische Resilienz durch Medien- und Digitalkompetenz gefördert werden kann, um die Gesellschaften in die Lage zu versetzen, sich an die sich wandelnden technologischen, politischen und gesellschaftlichen Herausforderungen anzupassen und zu gedeihen.
  • Die Bürgerinnen und Bürger sind in der Lage, die digitale Landschaft mit Unterscheidungsvermögen und kritischem Denken zu navigieren, aktiv mit den Medien und anderen Informationsquellen zu interagieren und eine informierte demokratische Teilhabe sicherzustellen.

Anwendungsbereich:

In dem Bericht „Sicherer zusammen“[1] wird darauf hingewiesen, dass die Kommission in den letzten Jahren bereits Maßnahmen ergriffen hat, um hybriden Bedrohungen (einschließlich ausländischer Informationsmanipulation und Einflussnahme/FIMI) entgegenzuwirken und die demokratische Resilienz in der gesamten EU zu stärken. Er nahm unter anderem den Europäischen Aktionsplan für Demokratie [2] an, um durch die Förderung freier und fairer Wahlen, die Stärkung der Medienfreiheit, die Bekämpfung von Desinformation und FIMI und die Förderung der Informationsintegrität widerstandsfähigere Demokratien in der gesamten EU aufzubauen. Mit der Annahme des Gesetzes über digitale Dienste [3] und seinen verbindlichen Verpflichtungen für Online-Plattformen zur Bekämpfung der Verbreitung von Desinformation hat die Kommission auch den Verhaltenskodex zur Bekämpfung von Desinformation gestärkt, der im Rahmen des Gesetzes über digitale Dienste zu einem Verhaltenskodex wurde. Darüber hinaus wurde durch die Einrichtung der Europäischen Beobachtungsstelle für digitale Medien (EDMO) und ihrer Hubs die Kapazität zur Aufdeckung, Analyse und Aufdeckung von Desinformationskampagnen erhöht.“[4]

In der Strategie für die Vorsorgeunion [5] wird hervorgehoben, dass die Vorsorge eine kollektive Verantwortung ist. Er weist auch darauf hin, dass unsere Demokratien widerstandsfähiger werden müssen, insbesondere im Hinblick auf die Stärkung des Vertrauens in die Institutionen, was in Krisensituationen, wie sie beispielsweise während der COVID-19-Pandemie zu beobachten waren, von entscheidender Bedeutung sein kann. Besonders schutzbedürftige Gruppen wie Kinder, Senioren und Menschen mit Behinderungen, ethnische oder religiöse Minderheiten, LGBTIQ-Personen, Menschen, die unter Armut und/oder sozialer Ausgrenzung leiden, sind unverhältnismäßig stark von Krisen betroffen und verschärfen häufig bereits bestehende Benachteiligungen, Hindernisse und Ungleichheiten.

Desinformation ist besonders schädlich, da sie das Vertrauen der Öffentlichkeit untergräbt und die Auswirkungen von Krisen verschärfen kann. Engagierte, informierte und gestärkte Bürgerinnen und Bürger sind die beste Garantie für die Widerstandsfähigkeit unserer Demokratien. Behörden, Schulen, Universitäten und Ausbildungseinrichtungen, Jugendinitiativen, Organisationen und Vereinigungen der Zivilgesellschaft, Sozialpartner, Unternehmen, lokale Netzwerke und Gemeinschaften sowie Bürgerinnen und Bürger von klein auf spielen bei diesen gemeinsamen Bemühungen eine entscheidende Rolle, und die vorgeschlagene Forschung sollte einen Multi-Akteurs-Ansatz verfolgen.

Vor diesem Hintergrund sollte die vorgeschlagene Forschung die komplexen und dynamischen Muster des Nutzerverhaltens im digitalen Zeitalter untersuchen und untersuchen, wie Einzelpersonen Informationen online und offline suchen, bewerten und mit ihnen interagieren. Eine solche Untersuchung wird von einer Analyse der emotionalen Dynamik bei der Verbreitung von Desinformation und Polarisierung auf digitalen Plattformen profitieren. Dies ist besonders relevant in Krisenkontexten, in denen ausländische Informationsmanipulation und Desinformation genutzt werden können, um Panik und Verwirrung zu verstärken. Die Vorschläge sollten untersuchen, wie Algorithmen emotionale Inhalte verstärken, Polarisierung fördern und das Vertrauen in demokratische Institutionen untergraben, sowie Krisenreaktion und entwickeln digitale und Medienkompetenzstrategien, um emotional manipulativen Narrativen wie populistischen und postfaktischen Diskursen entgegenzuwirken.

In der Forschung sollten auch die Faktoren untersucht werden, die die digitale Kompetenz, die Gewohnheiten der Informationssuche und das Online-Engagement beeinflussen, wobei der Schwerpunkt auf der Verbesserung der Beteiligung und des Engagements der Bürger durch digitale Mittel (auch durch Bürgertechnologie) und fundierte Entscheidungsfindung liegen sollte. In einer Zeit, in der Desinformation verwendet wird, um Zwietracht zu säen, indem die Ängste der Bürger ausgenutzt werden, ist es von entscheidender Bedeutung sicherzustellen, dass demokratische Entscheidungen von den zuverlässigsten und am weitesten akzeptierten verfügbaren Fakten und Informationsquellen beeinflusst werden. Die Forschung sollte die entscheidende Rolle untersuchen, die digitale und Medienkompetenz bei der Förderung der gesellschaftlichen Resilienz und der Informationsintegrität spielen können, indem es den Bürgerinnen und Bürgern ermöglicht wird, Fehlinformationen und Desinformation zu navigieren und zu widerstehen.

In den Vorschlägen sollte eine kritische Bewertung von Medien- und Digitalkompetenzinitiativen [6] geplant werden, um zu bewerten, ob die bestehenden Bemühungen die Widerstandsfähigkeit der Bürgerinnen und Bürger stärken oder ob neue Ansätze erforderlich sind, um die Bürgerinnen und Bürger wirksamer gegen sich entwickelnde Manipulationstaktiken auszurüsten.

Die Forschung sollte Strategien zur Verbesserung der Medienkompetenz und der digitalen und Medienkompetenz ermitteln, um kritisches Denken zu fördern, eine faktengestützte Entscheidungsfindung zu fördern und den negativen Auswirkungen von Desinformation auf demokratische Gesellschaften entgegenzuwirken. Um die Entwicklung praktischer Lösungen für Pädagogen und politische Entscheidungsträger zu erleichtern, könnte die Forschung computergestützte Instrumente wie die Analyse sozialer Netzwerke und die Verarbeitung natürlicher Sprache nutzen, um die Verbreitung von Desinformation über mehrere Plattformen hinweg abzubilden und einzudämmen. Dazu gehört die Identifizierung von koordiniertem unauthentischem Verhalten und die Analyse sowohl textlicher als auch visueller Inhalte, um Initiativen zur Medienkompetenz zu unterstützen.

Die Vorschläge werden ermutigt, andere relevante EU-finanzierte Projekte im Zusammenhang mit Medien- und Digitalkompetenz zu ermitteln und mögliche Möglichkeiten der Zusammenarbeit mit ihnen auszuloten. Clusterbildung und Zusammenarbeit mit anderen ausgewählten Projekten zu diesem Thema und anderen relevanten Projekten werden nachdrücklich gefördert.

Die für eine Finanzierung ausgewählten Projekte werden ermutigt, mit der GFS zusammenzuarbeiten, um Synergien mit ihrer Arbeit im Bereich Innovation für Demokratie und öffentliche Verwaltung zu suchen.

[1] https://commission.europa.eu/topics/defence/safer-together-path-towards-fully-prepared-union_en (auf Englisch)

[2] https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/de/ip_20_2250

[3] https://commission.europa.eu/strategy-and-policy/priorities-2019-2024/europe-fit-digital-age/digital-services-act_en (Deutsche Übersetzung)

[4] https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/de/policies/european-digital-media-observatory (Beobachtungsstelle für digitale Medien)

[5] Gemeinsame Mitteilung an das Europäische Parlament, den Europäischen Rat, den Rat, den Europäischen Wirtschafts- und Sozialausschuss und den Ausschuss der Regionen über die Strategie der Europäischen Vorsorgeunion

[6] Zum Beispiel „Guidelines for teachers and educators on tackle disinformation and promote digital literacy through education and training“, Amt für Veröffentlichungen der Europäischen Union, 2022, https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2766/28248; oder die „Global Standards for Media and Information Literacy Curricula Development Guidelines“ der UNESCO.

supportInfo:
Das Online-Handbuch ist Ihr Leitfaden für die Verfahren von der Einreichung von Vorschlägen bis zur Verwaltung Ihrer Finanzhilfe.

Der Programmleitfaden für „Horizont Europa“ enthält detaillierte Leitlinien zu Struktur, Haushalt und politischen Prioritäten von „Horizont Europa“.

Häufig gestellte Fragen zum Ausschreibungsportal – finden Sie Antworten auf die am häufigsten gestellten Fragen zur Einreichung von Vorschlägen, Bewertung und Verwaltung von Finanzhilfen.

Dienst für Forschungsanfragen – Fragen zu allen Aspekten der europäischen Forschung im Allgemeinen und zu den EU-Forschungsrahmenprogrammen im Besonderen stellen.

Nationale Kontaktstellen – Beratung, praktische Informationen und Unterstützung bei der Teilnahme an „Horizont Europa“. Darüber hinaus gibt es nationale Kontaktstellen in vielen Nicht-EU-Ländern und nicht assoziierten Ländern (im Folgenden „Drittländer“).

Enterprise Europe Network – wenden Sie sich an Ihren nationalen EEN-Kontakt, um Unternehmen mit besonderem Schwerpunkt auf KMU zu beraten. Die Unterstützung umfasst Leitlinien zur EU-Forschungsförderung.

IT-Helpdesk – wenden Sie sich an den IT-Helpdesk von Funding & Tenders Portal für Fragen wie vergessene Passwörter, Zugangsrechte und -rollen, technische Aspekte der Einreichung von Vorschlägen usw.

Der European IPR Helpdesk unterstützt Sie in Fragen des geistigen Eigentums.

CEN-CENELEC Research Helpdesk und ETSI Research Helpdesk – die europäischen Normungsorganisationen beraten Sie, wie Sie die Normung in Ihrem Projektvorschlag angehen können.

Die Europäische Charta für Forscher und der Verhaltenskodex für ihre Einstellung – konsultieren Sie die allgemeinen Grundsätze und Anforderungen, in denen die Rollen, Zuständigkeiten und Ansprüche von Forschern, Arbeitgebern und Geldgebern von Forschern festgelegt sind.

Die Partnersuche hilft Ihnen, eine Partnerorganisation für Ihr Angebot zu finden.

callTitle: Unterstützung der Umsetzung der Mission „Restore our Ocean and Waters“
descriptionByte:
Erwartetes Ergebnis:

Es wird erwartet, dass die Projektergebnisse zu allen folgenden erwarteten Ergebnissen beitragen:

  • Zusätzliche regionale und lokale Ressourcen (Daten, Modelle, digitale Zwillinge) werden auf der DTO-Kerninfrastruktur EDITO zur Verfügung gestellt;
  • neue Anwendungen des digitalen Zwillings, bei denen der Schwerpunkt auf regionalen und lokalen Gegebenheiten liegt und regionale Erwägungen berücksichtigt werden, einschließlich der Bedürfnisse der Interessenträger, der Verfügbarkeit von Daten usw.;
  • Stärkung der regionalen Fähigkeiten des digitalen Zwillings durch Schaffung der EU-DTO-Kerninfrastruktur, EDITO, der Bedingungen für die direkte Unterstützung der Umsetzung der Politik, einschließlich der Meeresumweltpolitik, und Anwendungen der blauen Wirtschaft, die auf den regionalen Merkmalen des Meeresbeckens aufbauen;
  • Entwicklung regionaler Was-wäre-wenn-Szenarien-Bibliotheken, einschließlich Konfidenzschwellen und damit zusammenhängender Analysen, Quantifizierung der notwendigen Bedingungen zur Erhöhung des Konfidenzniveaus usw.;
  • Unterstützung der Überwachung und nachhaltigen Bewirtschaftung regionaler Meere mit neuen maßgeschneiderten Diensten für regionale Meere.

Anwendungsbereich:

In den Vorschlägen sollten regionale Komponenten innerhalb der EDITO-Kerninfrastruktur des digitalen Zwillings des Ozeans der EU (EU DTO) festgelegt werden. Diese regionalen Komponenten sollten die Entwicklung lokaler Anwendungen digitaler Zwillinge fördern: maßgeschneiderte digitale Instrumente, die auf die einzigartigen Prioritäten spezifischer lokaler Stakeholder-Gemeinschaften zugeschnitten sind.

Für jedes Meeresbecken (ein Projekt pro Leuchtturm) besteht das Ziel darin,

  • Ermittlung, Aggregation und Integration bestehender regionaler Daten (über EMODnet), Instrumente, Modellierung und lokaler digitaler Zwillingsanlagen, die noch nicht weit verbreitet sind (einschließlich Binnengewässeranlagen, die für den integrierten Quell-zu-Meer-Ansatz mit Schwerpunkt auf Land-Meer-Verbindungen [1] relevant sind), und Ergreifen der erforderlichen Maßnahmen, um sie über EDITO unter Einhaltung aller erforderlichen Interoperabilitäts- und Normungsprotokolle zur Verfügung zu stellen. Von besonderem Interesse sind unterrepräsentierte Datentypen (Biologging, akustische Telemetrie usw.);
  • Entwicklung regionaler digitaler Zwillingsdienste (maßgeschneiderte Anwendungen und Dienste zur Bewältigung regionaler Herausforderungen, z. B. Herausforderungen für kleine Inseln, Küstenresilienz, Erhaltung und Wiederherstellung der biologischen Vielfalt, Umweltverschmutzung, Anpassung an den Klimawandel, Fischerei und Aquakultur und andere Sektoren der blauen Wirtschaft). Diese Dienste sollten sich sowohl auf politikrelevante Fragen als auch auf Fragen im Zusammenhang mit der Entwicklung einer nachhaltigen und wettbewerbsfähigen blauen Wirtschaft in der Region konzentrieren. Zur Unterstützung prädiktiver Kapazitäten sollten regionale Entwicklungen des digitalen Zwillings insbesondere auf die Integration langfristiger Datensätze zur Überwachung der Umwelt und der biologischen Vielfalt abzielen, um sicherzustellen, dass Modellierungen und Szenarien auf empirischen Beobachtungen in Zeitreihen beruhen;
  • Förderung der Einbeziehung regionaler Interessenträger (Regionalbehörden, regionale Meeresübereinkommen, Industriepartner und lokale Gemeinschaften), um vorhandene Ressourcen (Datenbanken, lokale oder regionale Modelle) zur gemeinsamen Gestaltung und Validierung von Anwendungen des digitalen Zwillings für eine wirksame Politikgestaltung und operative Entscheidungsunterstützung zu nutzen;
  • Verbesserung der intensiven Einführung innovativer Algorithmen der künstlichen Intelligenz und des Big-Data-Managements;
  • Entwickeln Sie durch das oben genannte Engagement und durch Co-Creation-Prozesse eine Reihe von Was-wäre-wenn-Szenarien, bewerten Sie ihr Vertrauensniveau und identifizieren Sie Maßnahmen zur Verbesserung dieses Vertrauens.

[1] Zum Beispiel Vermögenswerte, die in der IDEATION CSA identifiziert und unter „HORIZON-MISS-2023-OCEAN-01-09 towards the integration of inland waters into the Digital Twin Ocean“ finanziert wurden. https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101157371

supportInfo:
Das Online-Handbuch ist Ihr Leitfaden für die Verfahren von der Einreichung von Vorschlägen bis zur Verwaltung Ihrer Finanzhilfe.

Der Programmleitfaden für „Horizont Europa“ enthält detaillierte Leitlinien zu Struktur, Haushalt und politischen Prioritäten von „Horizont Europa“.

Häufig gestellte Fragen zum Ausschreibungsportal – finden Sie Antworten auf die am häufigsten gestellten Fragen zur Einreichung von Vorschlägen, Bewertung und Verwaltung von Finanzhilfen.

Dienst für Forschungsanfragen – Fragen zu allen Aspekten der europäischen Forschung im Allgemeinen und zu den EU-Forschungsrahmenprogrammen im Besonderen stellen.

Nationale Kontaktstellen – Beratung, praktische Informationen und Unterstützung bei der Teilnahme an „Horizont Europa“. Darüber hinaus gibt es nationale Kontaktstellen in vielen Nicht-EU-Ländern und nicht assoziierten Ländern (im Folgenden „Drittländer“).

Enterprise Europe Network – wenden Sie sich an Ihren nationalen EEN-Kontakt, um Unternehmen mit besonderem Schwerpunkt auf KMU zu beraten. Die Unterstützung umfasst Leitlinien zur EU-Forschungsförderung.

IT-Helpdesk – wenden Sie sich an den IT-Helpdesk von Funding & Tenders Portal für Fragen wie vergessene Passwörter, Zugangsrechte und -rollen, technische Aspekte der Einreichung von Vorschlägen usw.

Der European IPR Helpdesk unterstützt Sie in Fragen des geistigen Eigentums.

CEN-CENELEC Research Helpdesk und ETSI Research Helpdesk – die europäischen Normungsorganisationen beraten Sie, wie Sie die Normung in Ihrem Projektvorschlag angehen können.

Die Europäische Charta für Forscher und der Verhaltenskodex für ihre Einstellung – konsultieren Sie die allgemeinen Grundsätze und Anforderungen, in denen die Rollen, Zuständigkeiten und Ansprüche von Forschern, Arbeitgebern und Geldgebern von Forschern festgelegt sind.

Die Partnersuche hilft Ihnen, eine Partnerorganisation für Ihr Angebot zu finden.

title: Validarea operațională la scară largă și extinderea instrumentelor și modelelor IA (generative) de ultimă generație care alimentează un sistem energetic digital de generație următoare
destinationDetails:
Această destinație include activități care vizează o aprovizionare cu energie durabilă, sigură și competitivă. În conformitate cu domeniul de aplicare al clusterului 5, aceasta include activități în domeniul energiei din surse regenerabile; sistemul energetic, rețelele și stocarea; precum și captarea, utilizarea și stocarea dioxidului de carbon (CUSC).

Această destinație contribuie în mod direct la orientările strategice esențiale ale planului strategic „Tranziția verde”,„Tranziția digitală” și „O Europă mai rezilientă, mai competitivă, mai favorabilă incluziunii și mai democratică”.

În conformitate cu planul strategic, impactul global preconizat al acestei destinații este de a contribui la „asigurarea unei aprovizionări cu energie mai durabile, mai sigure și mai competitive prin soluții pentru sisteme energetice inteligente bazate pe soluții în materie de energie din surse regenerabile”.

Această destinație contribuie la activitățile Planului strategic european privind tehnologiile energetice (Planul SET) și ale grupurilor de lucru pentru punerea în aplicare a acestuia.

Principalele impacturi care urmează să fie generate de subiectele din cadrul acestei destinații sunt:

Energia din surse regenerabile

  1. Producătorii de energie au acces la tehnologii europene eficiente și competitive în domeniul energiei din surse regenerabile și al combustibililor din surse regenerabile, cu o bază solidă de cunoștințe, și sunt în măsură să le implementeze pentru a spori securitatea energetică a UE și pentru a-și atinge obiectivele de neutralitate climatică, într-un mod durabil din punct de vedere ecologic (de exemplu, biodiversitate, utilizări multiple ale terenurilor și apei, resurse naturale, poluare) și socioeconomic și în conformitate cu obiectivele de dezvoltare durabilă.
  2. Furnizorii de tehnologie au acces la lanțuri valorice europene competitive, reziliente, fiabile, durabile și la prețuri accesibile ale energiei din surse regenerabile și ale tehnologiilor bazate pe combustibili din surse regenerabile, inclusiv la cele emergente, și au un potențial puternic de export pentru a aproviziona atât piața internă a UE, cât și piața mondială. Acestea beneficiază, de asemenea, de tehnologii circulare în domeniul energiei din surse regenerabile care sunt sigure și sustenabile prin concepție, cu o dependență externă redusă și diversificată de materiile prime critice [1].
  3. Sectoarele economice beneficiază de o mai bună integrare a energiei din surse regenerabile și a soluțiilor bazate pe combustibili din surse regenerabile care sunt, printre altele, competitive, eficiente din punctul de vedere al costurilor, eficiente, flexibile, fiabile și durabile. O astfel de integrare este facilitată prin digitalizarea și integrarea inteligenței artificiale a tehnologiilor din domeniul energiei din surse regenerabile care asigură stabilitatea și fiabilitatea rețelei.
  4. Industriile europene beneficiază de un potențial consolidat de export al tehnologiilor din domeniul energiei din surse regenerabile și al combustibililor din surse regenerabile, inclusiv prin parteneriate internaționale, și devin mai competitive în ceea ce privește tehnologiile inovatoare din domeniul energiei din surse regenerabile în Europa și la nivel mondial.
  5. Cercetătorii europeni beneficiază de o comunitate mai puternică și de o bază științifică consolidată privind energia din surse regenerabile și tehnologiile bazate pe combustibili din surse regenerabile, inclusiv cele emergente, inclusiv prin colaborări internaționale.
  6. Cetățenii europeni au acces la o piață a energiei care este corectă și echitabilă, mai rezilientă, utilizează toate tipurile diferite de resurse regenerabile locale de energie și este mai puțin dependentă de importurile de combustibili fosili. Cetățenii se confruntă cu mai puțină sărăcie energetică și de combustibil și beneficiază, de asemenea, de noi oportunități de ocupare a forței de muncă și de perfecționare. Comunitățile locale beneficiază de un sistem energetic mai descentralizat, mai accesibil și mai sigur și de utilizări multiple ale terenurilor și apei.

Sisteme energetice, rețele și stocare

  1. Acțiunile de C&Amp;I vor sprijini transformarea digitală și verde justă a sistemului energetic prin soluții avansate pentru accelerarea integrării sistemelor energetice și a decarbonizării. Soluțiile curate și durabile dezvoltate vor contribui la o mai bună funcționare a sistemului energetic pentru actori și la furnizarea de energie mai fiabilă, rezilientă și sigură – chiar și în cazul unor fenomene climatice extreme din ce în ce mai frecvente.
  2. Soluțiile dezvoltate vor contribui la creșterea flexibilității și a capacității de găzduire a rețelelor pentru sursele regenerabile de energie prin optimizarea integrării transsectoriale și a stocării la scară de rețea, precum și prin acoperirea situațiilor din afara rețelei. Acestea vor îmbunătăți gradul de pregătire a sistemului de energie electrică pentru a sprijini obiectivul obligatoriu al UE pentru 2030 de minimum 42,5 % energie din surse regenerabile în consumul final brut de energie (cu aspirația de a atinge 45 %) și decarbonizarea completă până în 2050. Acestea vor permite electrificarea în continuare a cererii și vor spori competitivitatea lanțului valoric european, vor reduce presiunea asupra resurselor (inclusiv prin transformarea tehnologiilor în tehnologii „circulare prin concepție”) și vor reduce dependențele. Astfel de soluții ar permite, de asemenea, o mai bună reziliență a UE la riscurile climatice.
  3. Soluțiile vor îmbunătăți sensibilizarea și implicarea consumatorilor în tranziția energetică, prin oferte și servicii inovatoare (de exemplu, răspunsul părții de consum, comunitățile energetice) și vor viza diferite tipuri de consumatori, inclusiv grupurile de populație „greu accesibile” (cum ar fi gospodăriile sărace din punct de vedere energetic sau cu venituri mici). Acest lucru va duce la creșterea încrederii în noile produse și servicii care intră în sistemul energetic și la adoptarea acestora.

Captarea, utilizarea și stocarea dioxidului de carbon (CUSC) și eliminarea dioxidului de carbon (CDR)

  1. Implementarea accelerată a captării, utilizării și stocării dioxidului de carbon (CUSC) ca opțiune de atenuare a emisiilor de CO2 în producția de energie electrică și/sau în aplicațiile industriale, precum și eliminarea dioxidului de carbon pentru emisiile negative.

Entitățile juridice stabilite în China nu sunt eligibile să participe atât la acțiunile de cercetare și inovare, cât și la acțiunile de inovare care se încadrează în această destinație. Pentru informații suplimentare, a se vedea „Restricții privind participarea entităților juridice stabilite în China”, care figurează în anexa B generală la anexele generale.

[1] Pentru un exemplu de metodologie de evaluare a durabilității, a circularității și a contribuției la reziliența și autonomia tehnologică a UE în ceea ce privește tehnologiile energetice curate în cadrul rezervei de C&Amp, a se vedea Studiul privind abordările circulare pentru o tranziție către o energie curată durabilă și la prețuri accesibile.
descriptionByte:
Rezultatul preconizat:

Se preconizează că rezultatele proiectului vor contribui la toate rezultatele preconizate următoare:

  • Instrumente avansate și sigure de IA (eficiente din punctul de vedere al energiei, al resurselor, al datelor și al costurilor, durabile) pentru operațiunile în timp real ale rețelei (inclusiv protecția), operațiunile de piață (dacă este cazul) și capacitarea consumatorilor în sistemele energetice distribuite.
  • Un mediu demonstrat de dezvoltare a IA, integrat cu coloana vertebrală digitală modernizată a sistemului energetic și cu aplicații pentru consumatori care economisesc energie.
  • Capacități extinse de învățare la noduri periferice și sisteme federate care utilizează arhitecturi bazate pe agenți.
  • Un cadru de guvernanță și un model de operare pentru coloana vertebrală digitală alimentată de Gen(AI).

Domeniul de aplicare:

Pe baza acțiunilor anterioare din cadrul programului Orizont Europa (de exemplu, coloana vertebrală digitală a sistemului energetic din clusterul 5, precum și activitățile de cloud și edge continuum și activitățile de prelucrare a datelor IA din clusterul 4) și Europa digitală (Cadrul comun de referință pentru aplicațiile consumatorilor de energie din întreaga UE, spațiul comun al datelor privind energia), se preconizează că proiectele:

  1. Validați (amplasamentul demo și rețeaua operațională) și scalați instrumente și modele de IA cu sursă deschisă (generative) sigure și de ultimă generație (eficiente din punct de vedere energetic și al utilizării resurselor, eficiente din punctul de vedere al datelor și al costurilor, implementate la nivel local și durabile) pentru monitorizarea, echilibrarea, prognozarea și capacitarea consumatorilor în timp real în cadrul unui sistem energetic distribuit.
  2. Demonstrarea unui mediu de dezvoltare a IA în coloana vertebrală digitală îmbunătățită a sistemului energetic, inclusiv a geamănului său digital, care ar trebui să includă funcționalitatea cadrului comun de referință pentru aplicațiile de economisire a energiei.
  3. Prototiparea și validarea la scară largă a învățării automate la nivelul nodurilor periferice și gruparea la nivel de roi într-o arhitectură bazată pe agenți, valorificând noi mecanisme pentru reducerea modelelor de IA, precum și învățarea incrementală și de consolidare.
  4. Rezultatele proiectului ar trebui să fie compatibile cu principiile spațiului european comun al datelor privind energia și în concordanță cu Busola UE privind aplicarea IA și competitivitatea, asigurându-se că acestea promovează adoptarea IA și competitivitatea în conformitate cu politicile UE, precum și digitalizarea UE a inițiativelor din sectorul energetic.
  5. Acolo unde este relevant și posibil, se preconizează că proiectele selectate vor utiliza fabricile și gigafabricile europene de IA.
  6. Se așteaptă ca proiectele selectate, în cazul în care sunt disponibile, să utilizeze și să dezvolte în continuare standardele europene convenite de comun acord și să colaboreze în mod activ și să contribuie la activitatea organizațiilor europene consacrate și de facto care elaborează standarde, precum și a comunităților și platformelor cu sursă deschisă.

Se preconizează că proiectele selectate vor contribui la inițiativa BRIDGE [1] și vor participa activ la activitățile acesteia.

Nivelul de pregătire tehnologică - Nivelul de pregătire tehnologică așteptat de la proiectele finalizate

Se preconizează că activitățile vor atinge TRL 7-8 până la sfârșitul proiectului – a se vedea anexa B generală. Activitățile pot începe la orice TRL.

[1] https://bridge-smart-grid-storage-systems-digital-projects.ec.europa.eu/

Manualul online este ghidul dumneavoastră privind procedurile de la depunerea propunerii până la gestionarea grantului.

Ghidul programului Orizont Europa conține orientări detaliate privind structura, bugetul și prioritățile politice ale programului Orizont Europa.

Funding & Tenders Portal FAQ – găsiți răspunsurile la cele mai frecvente întrebări privind depunerea propunerilor, evaluarea și gestionarea granturilor.

Serviciul de informare în domeniul cercetării – adresați întrebări cu privire la orice aspect al cercetării europene în general și al programelor-cadru de cercetare ale UE în special.

Punctele naționale de contact (PCN) – obțineți orientări, informații practice și asistență cu privire la participarea la programul Orizont Europa. Există, de asemenea, puncte de contact naționale în multe țări din afara UE și țări neasociate („țări terțe”).

Rețeaua întreprinderilor europene – contactați contactul național EEN pentru consilierea întreprinderilor, cu un accent special pe IMM-uri. Sprijinul include orientări privind finanțarea cercetării de către UE.

Serviciul de asistență informatică – contactați serviciul de asistență informatică al Portalului pentru licitații pentru întrebări precum parolele uitate, drepturile și rolurile de acces, aspectele tehnice ale depunerii propunerilor etc.

Serviciul european de asistență în materie de DPI vă oferă asistență cu privire la aspecte legate de proprietatea intelectuală.

CEN-CENELEC Research Helpdesk și ETSI Research Helpdesk – organizațiile europene de standardizare vă sfătuiesc cum să abordați standardizarea în propunerea dumneavoastră de proiect.

Carta europeană a cercetătorilor și Codul de conduită pentru recrutarea acestora – consultați principiile și cerințele generale care specifică rolurile, responsabilitățile și drepturile cercetătorilor, ale angajatorilor și ale finanțatorilor cercetătorilor.

Căutarea de parteneri vă ajută să găsiți o organizație parteneră pentru propunerea dvs.

results.content: Digital enablers and building blocks for collaborative Earth Observation and Satellite telecommunications for Space solutions (Space Partnership)

destinationDetails:
Today, EU citizens enjoy watching satellite TV, increasingly accurate global navigation services for all transport modes and users, extended Earth monitoring for land, marine, atmosphere and climate change, global meteorological observation and accurate cartographies of a wide number of variables. Space also makes important contributions to security crisis management and emergency services. The EU Space Programme components (such as EGNSS and Copernicus) are key assets for the EU policies on climate, environment, transport, agriculture and secure society. Finally, the Space sector is a source of economic growth and jobs.

This Destination is structured along the following building blocks:

  • Accessing Space, i.e. the ability to transport satellites, cargo, and humans into space; build and launch the required vehicles, including re-usable systems; and operate the related facilities and services.
  • Using Space on Earth, i.e. the ability to provide space-based secure communication, navigation and Earth observation services and applications, including through the EU Space flagships Galileo, Copernicus and IRIS2.
  • Monitoring Space, i.e. the ability to detect, track and anticipate the trajectory of spacecraft, Near-Earth objects, and space debris during their full lifetime; to share data with relevant stakeholders; and to provide solutions for safe international space traffic management. It also includes the tracking and anticipation of other impacts on the space environment, such as Space weather events.
  • Acting in Space, i.e. the ability to inspect, rendezvous and dock, grasp, repair, refuel, reconfigure, build, assemble and disassemble, reuse/recycle, relocate, remove and transport operational, non-operational, and other objects in space, including platforms or larger structures.
  • Exploring Space, i.e. the ability to conduct high profile space exploration activities, perform excellent science and exploit space data to increase our knowledge about the Universe and celestial bodies, with a view to their exploration for scientific and socio-economic benefits.
  • Boosting Space, i.e. the ability to sustain the above strategic capabilities through fostering the competitiveness of the EU space sector; improving education and developing the required skills; accelerating the pace of innovation; supporting EU non-dependency on critical technologies; and strengthening international cooperation.

Those building blocks are implemented through the following headings:

  • Heading 1: Accessing Space

Autonomous access to space is a prerequisite for the strategic autonomy of the EU. It is a key enabler and indispensable element in the space ecosystem and value chain. European launch systems allow the autonomous deployment of satellites for the Union’s flagships Copernicus, Galileo/EGNOS and IRIS2 and contribute to the security and resilience of Europe’s sovereign space infrastructure.

In a context of fierce competition and launch services paradigm changes, ensuring that Europe improves the resilience and the cost-effectiveness of its autonomous access to space is crucial. This requires urgent activities to enable and further consolidate operational capacities before 2030 in line with the Strategic R&I Agenda for EU-funded Space research supporting competitiveness adopted in 2020.

This challenge will be tackled by fostering space transportation solutions through the support to building blocks for smart technologies and digital solutions and through facilitating access to European spaceports.

  • Heading 2: Acting in Space

In-Space Operations and Services (ISOS) will ensure EU’s freedom of action in space and increase the resilience, sustainability, safety and protection of its space infrastructure, and contribute to the strengthening of the competitiveness of its space sector. R&I activities should bring Europe to the forefront of emerging service applications, including inspection, rendezvous and docking, grasping, repair, reconfiguration, assembly and disassembly, manufacturing, resource extraction, reuse/recycling, removal and transport of objects in space, for satellites, platforms and larger structures. Key space R&I activities will be driven by a pilot mission that will contribute to establish and foster a new in-space economy.

Game-changing innovations and enabling technologies are at the heart of ISOS and an important focus of future actions. The paradigm shift towards adaptive space systems builds on automation and robotics, artificial intelligence, modular and reconfigurable spacecraft concepts. Together with other enabling technologies such as electric propulsion, intelligent mechanisms and interfaces or advanced GNC, they will provide new ways on how space assets are designed, produced, tested, transported, and operated. Different means realised with AppStore-like approaches will benefit the future space ecosystem and foster a circular economy.

  • Heading 3: Using Space on Earth related to telecommunications

The Union Secure Connectivity programme aims to develop a secure and autonomous space-based connectivity system for the provision of guaranteed and resilient satellite communications on Earth. Among the objectives are to develop, build and operate a multiorbital space-based state-of-the-art connectivity system, continuously adapted to governmental satellite communications demand evolution; to complement the Union pool of satellite communication capacities and services; and to integrate the GOVSATCOM ground segment infrastructure, as well as the European quantum communication infrastructure (EuroQCI).

In the context of the co-Programmed European Partnership for Globally Competitive Space Systems (Space Partnership), R&I will focus on cohesive activities in the domain of digital developments under the grand heading of Digitalisation for Commercial Space solutions, more specifically on collaborative and synergetic solutions for Earth Observation and Satellite Telecommunication missions.

  • Heading 4: Using Space on Earth related to Earth Observation

The evolution of Copernicus core services (Climate Change, Marine Environment Monitoring, Land Monitoring, Atmosphere Monitoring, Emergency Management and Security) is being taken care of through projects launched under the previous R&I work programmes.

In the context of the co-Programmed European Partnership for Globally Competitive Space Systems (Space Partnership), R&I will focus on cohesive activities in the domain of digital developments under the grand heading of Digitalisation for Commercial Space solutions, more specifically on collaborative and synergetic solutions for Earth Observation and Satellite Telecommunication missions.

In addition, we will strive to also support the development of innovative applications of Copernicus’ services and data. That said, such support is also coming from non-HE activities carried out by EUSPA, the EU agency for the Space Programme: collaboration with receivers’ manufacturers, with mobile phones’ manufacturers, with cars’ manufacturers, etc., as well as through influencing the development of policies where the use of Earth Observation data is required.

  • Heading 5: Using Space on Earth related to satellite navigation

For Galileo/EGNOS, the international context, the competitive environment with emerging actors including from the private sector, novel techniques in the value chain such as LEO layer for PNT or ground segment automation based on Artificial Intelligence, the increasing threats in space and in cyber, and the evolution of the technologies, components and systems, call for a constant adaptation of the EU space infrastructure to these changing realities.

To meet these challenges, EU needs sustained investments in R&D for innovative mission concepts, technology and systems. These will ensure the continuity of the EGNSS service, minimise the risks for technology inclusion in the infrastructure, thanks to anticipated development and testing including in-orbit, and protect better this infrastructure against modern threats (notably cyber, jamming/spoofing, natural hazards).

These investments in R&D will contribute to maintaining the EU´s leadership position in the Global Navigation Satellite Systems, and to strengthening the strategic autonomy of the EU.

In addition, we will strive to also support the development of innovative applications of EGNSS’ services and data. That said, such support is also coming from non-HE activities carried out by EUSPA, the EU agency for the Space Programme: collaboration with receivers’ manufacturers, with mobile phones’ manufacturers, with cars’ manufacturers, etc., as well as through influencing the development of policies where the use of satellite navigation data is required.

  • Heading 6: Space sciences and exploration

Space sciences and exploration are important areas that must be fostered for various reasons, focusing on where the EU can add value with limited financial means. Firstly, it is key to capitalise on Europe’s investments in space missions and exploit data coming from European space missions (including demonstration and validation). This should lay the grounds for future exploration missions. Furthermore, such focus on sciences will strengthen the position of leading European scientists and also animate societal interest in space. Last but not least, it will expand human knowledge and the natural curiosity of mankind.

  • Heading 7: Monitoring Space

Orbital space infrastructure, the data, and the services they deliver have become indispensable for European societies and economies and in the daily lives of Europeans. However, due to an increasingly congested orbital space, the likelihood of a satellite being severely damaged or destroyed in a collision has raised dramatically. Such risk calls for action to preserve European interests by protecting its private and public investments in space in a sustainable manner.

Based on the EU Space Programme, capabilities of the Space Situational Awareness (SSA) component and Space Surveillance and Tracking (SST) services are being developed and consolidated through a Partnership of 15 Member States. The EU SST Partnership Agreement has entered into force on 11 November 2022. With this Partnership, EU SST builds on the good results achieved by the initial consortium of 5 Member States and targets continuity of activities and service provision, improvement of specialisation on expertise, and consideration of the duality and security dimension of SST.

EU SST relies on the European industry, including start-ups, to develop and improve national, public-owned capacities based on Partnership’s requirements. In the pursuit of EU strategic autonomy, both as regards the need to protect EU space infrastructures and as regards the need to strengthen EU SST capabilities, research and development activities are aiming the enhancement and consolidation of EU SST autonomy in all orbital zones beyond the existing network of national assets, counting on MS contributions and leveraging complementary contributions from European private capabilities and commercial initiatives.

Importantly, SSA also covers the domains of Space Weather (SW) and Near-Earth Objects (NEO). For those domains, activities are ongoing and no additional ones are needed under the 2026-2027 WP.

  • Heading 8: Boosting space through EU non-dependence for key critical space technologies

Ensuring non-dependence for critical space technologies is key, especially in the current geo-political context. The European Commission has undertaken several activities and deployed new tools (e.g. the EU Observatory of Critical Technologies) for assessing space technologies and identify those that are critical from a dependency point of view. Within this domain, a number of technological developments will be initiated with focus on priorities stemming from on-going and planned EU Space missions, including IRIS2. Emphasis will be on reducing non-EU dependencies on critical space technologies across their whole supply chain from advanced materials to components, equipment, and sub-systems; providing unrestricted access to advanced space technologies relevant for EU space missions and programme components; developing or regaining capacity to operate independently in space by developing resilient space technologies supply chains, relying on EU supply chains and/or trustable and reliable supply chains not affected by non-EU export restrictions; enhancing competitiveness by developing products and capabilities reaching equivalent or superior performance level than those from outside the EU and compete at worldwide level; and opening new opportunities for manufacturers by reducing dependency on export restricted technologies.

  • Heading 9: Boosting Space through innovative space technologies

Mastering quantum technologies is essential for EU technological sovereignty and their use in EU space missions will offer major improvements in the performance of the EU space systems. Their developments will contribute to EU leadership in this field, in particular quantum sensing technology based on quantum accelerometers, developed in the frame of the Quantum Space Gravimetry pathfinder mission.

  • Heading 10: Boosting Space through IOD/IOV opportunities

IOD/IOV opportunities continue to be needed for experiments needing aggregation as well as for read-to-fly satellites. This includes the Flight Ticket Initiative to support competitiveness and innovation of the European Space sector.

  • Heading 11: Boosting Space through support to entrepreneurship

Business development, acceleration and upscaling of start-ups is also much needed, which has given rise to the set-up of the CASSINI Space Entrepreneurship Initiative. CASSINI provides support to business and innovation-friendly ecosystems, including the strengthening business skills in the space market segments and digital services based on space data. CASSINI also aims at making start-ups and scale-ups investment-ready and able to secure venture capital funding and at leveraging synergies with the InvestEU programme and the EU Space Programme.

  • Heading 12: Boosting Space through support to the Space Act and cybersecurity

The interinstitutional discussions for the adoption of an EU Space Act will start as soon as the Commission has issued its proposal still in 2025. One adopted, it will be important to foresee some studies and assimilated activities to support its implementation. The same goes for the area of cybersecurity which has become extremely important also in the Space domain.

Limiting participation in certain actions to Member States (and certain associated countries to Horizon Europe)

The Space research part of the Horizon Europe Programme is by default open to the world, promoting international cooperation to drive scientific excellence.

However, an important aspect of this Destination consists in ensuring security and strengthening strategic autonomy across key technologies and value chains, taking advantage of the possibilities that space offers for the security of the Union and its Member States. This objective requires special rules in specific cases to set the requisite eligibility and participation conditions to ensure the protection of the integrity, security and resilience of the Union and its Member States. Hence, on an exceptional basis and duly justified, this work programme may foresee a limited participation to entities from selected countries. Such exceptional circumstances would relate to prevalent considerations to safeguard the Union’s strategic assets, interests, autonomy or security. Possibilities for such limitations are framed by Article 22(5) of the Horizon Europe Regulation.

Legal entities established in China are not eligible to participate in both Research and Innovation Actions (RIAs) and Innovation Actions (IAs) falling under this Destination. For additional information please see “Restrictions on the participation of legal entities established in China” found in General Annex B of the General Annexes.

The following call(s) in this work programme contribute to this destination:

HORIZON-CL4-2026-03-SPACE

HORIZON-CL4-2027-03-SPACE

HORIZON-CL4-2027-EUSPA-SPACE
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

The topic encompasses actions within the scope of the co-programmed European Partnership on Globally Competitive Space Systems (‘Space Partnership’) in the areas of satellite communication (SatCom), Earth Observation (EO) and New Commercial Space Transportation Solutions and is part of cohesive activities in the domain of digital developments under the grand heading of “digitalisation for commercial space solutions”.

Digitalisation is a major enabler for enhancing the value of an End-to-End EO and SatCom system. Under the area of Using Space on Earth related to SatCom and EO, below this topic focusses on the Low to Mid TRL level developments of key technologies[1] required to strengthen competitiveness in these domains with a dedicated focus on synergies between Earth observation and Satellite telecommunication technologies.

Projects are expected to contribute to one or several of the following outcomes:

  • Next generation Earth observation and SatCom payloads, technologies and processing means (on ground and in space);
  • Security of SatCom and EO services, supporting next-generation technologies for both ground and space commercial applications.

This will contribute to developing, deploying global, more flexible and reactive space-based services applications, to contribute to fostering the EU's space sector competitiveness, as stated in the expected impact of this destination.

Scope:

The areas of R&I, which needs to be addressed to tackle the above-mentioned expected outcomes are:

  • R&I on End-to-End SatCom Mission capabilities for increased robustness, energy efficient connectivity and compatibility with 5G & 6G waveforms such as constellation and network software management systems and optical communications, including both space and ground-based assets, and digital on-ground infrastructure to test and enhance operational efficiency;
  • R&I on building blocks and processes common to EO and SatCom systems allowing for in-orbit reconfigurability, faster data availability, on-board and on-ground smart computing and improved operation resilience.

Proposals are expected to promote cooperation between different actors (industry, SMEs, research institutions and infrastructures and academia) and consider opportunities to quickly turn technological innovation into commercial use in space.

It is expected that projects make use of existing EU technologies and/or building blocks, including at component level, contributing to EU non-dependence and strengthen competitiveness, and this should be clearly presented in the proposal. Furthermore, proposed activities should be complementary to H2020 and Horizon Europe funded projects, national activities and activities funded by the European Space Agency (ESA).

This topic contributes to the implementation of the European Partnership on ‘Globally Competitive Space Systems’ (GCSS).

In this topic, the integration of the gender dimension (sex and gender analysis) in research and innovation content should be addressed only if relevant in relation to the objectives of the research effort.

3. Other Eligible Conditions

If projects use satellite-based earth observation, positioning, navigation and/or related timing data and services, beneficiaries must make use of Copernicus and/or Galileo/EGNOS (other data and services may additionally be used).

In order to achieve the expected outcomes, and safeguard the Union’s strategic assets, interests, autonomy, and security, it is important to avoid a situation of technological dependency on a non-EU source, in a global context that requires the EU to take action to build on its strengths, and to carefully assess and address any strategic weaknesses, vulnerabilities and high-risk dependencies which put at risk the attainment of its ambitions. For this reason, participation is limited to legal entities established in Member States, Iceland and Norway and the following additional associated countries : Canada, New-Zealand, United Kingdom and Switzerland. In addition, entities established in third countries which may become associated to Horizon Europe during 2026 and 2027 may be eligible to participate in this topic if the third country is identified for this topic as an eligible country in the List of Participating Countries in Horizon Europe at the time of submission of the application[[See the List of Participating Countries in Horizon Europe available at https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/docs/2021-2027/common/guidance/list-3rd-country-participation_horizon-euratom_en.pdf.]]. In any case, the association agreement to the Programme must apply by the time of the signature of the grant agreement.

For the duly justified and exceptional reasons listed in the paragraph above, in order to guarantee the protection of the strategic interests of the Union and its Member States, entities established in an eligible country listed above, but which are directly or indirectly controlled by a non-eligible country or by a non-eligible country entity, may not participate in the action unless it can be demonstrated, by means of guarantees positively assessed by their eligible country of establishment, that their participation to the action would not negatively impact the Union’s strategic assets, interests, autonomy, or security. Entities assessed as high-risk suppliers of mobile network communication equipment within the meaning of ‘restrictions for the protection of European communication networks’ (or entities fully or partially owned or controlled by a high-risk supplier) cannot submit guarantees.[[ The guarantees shall in particular substantiate that, for the purpose of the action, measures are in place to ensure that: a) control over the applicant legal entity is not exercised in a manner that retrains or restricts its ability to carry out the action and to deliver results, that imposes restrictions concerning its infrastructure, facilities, assets, resources, intellectual property or know-how needed for the purpose of the action, or that undermines its capabilities and standards necessary to carry out the action; b) access by a non-eligible country or by a non-eligible country entity to sensitive information relating to the action is prevented; and the employees or other persons involved in the action have a national security clearance issued by an eligible country, where appropriate; c) ownership of the intellectual property arising from, and the results of, the action remain within the recipient during and after completion of the action, are not subject to control or restrictions by non-eligible countries or non-eligible country entity, and are not exported outside the eligible countries, nor is access to them from outside the eligible countries granted, without the approval of the eligible country in which the legal entity is established.]]

descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

Expected outcomes and deliverables are:

Work strand 1:

  1. Guidance for public authorities and healthcare providers to deploy, upgrade and operate digital health services and systems that support the rights of citizens and fulfil their obligations under the EHDS.
  2. Maintenance and expansion of a community of public authorities and healthcare providers based on common guidance for services and systems aligned with the objectives of the EHDS. The community should build upon one or more existing communities.
  3. Large-scale deployment of and/or capacity building for digital health services and systems that support the EEHRxF and the rights of citizens included in the EHDS.

Work strand 2:

  1. A toolbox for data holders to support dataset description, data quality and utility labelling, and secondary use readiness in alignment with the EHDS.
  2. Establishment or expansion of existing community of data holders with the objective of supporting peer exchange, reuse of good practices and alignment of approaches for the creation and maintenance of dataset descriptions and data quality and utility labels for secondary use under the EHDS.
  3. Creation of dataset descriptions and data quality and utility labelling by data holders, such as public authorities and healthcare providers.
  4. Integration of datasets descriptions in the datasets catalogues of health data access bodies.
  5. Support to data holders in putting in place the organisational and technical arrangements required to make electronic health data available for secondary use under the EHDS, in line with applicable safeguards.

Work strand 3:

  1. A training framework and training sessions to prepare service providers to support public authorities, healthcare providers and data holders in the implementation of the EHDS as described above, complementing and aligning with the work of the EEHRxF Support Centre, i2X Capacity Building for Secondary Use [1], and QUANTUM [2] .
  2. A business model, including the uptake strategy, for service providers that can support the adoption of the EEHRxF, the uptake of services and systems compatible with the EHDS and the creation and maintenance of dataset descriptions and data quality and utility labels.
  3. A community of trained service providers trained to support public authorities, healthcare providers and data holders in fulfilling requirements of the EHDS.

1 - https://hadea.ec.europa.eu/calls-tenders/capacity-building-secondary-uses-health-data-european-health-data-space_en

2 - https://quantumproject.eu/

Objective:

Regulation (EU) 2025/327 of the European Parliament and of the Council (‘The European Health Data Space (EHDS) Regulation’) [1] reinforces the rights for citizens to access and control their personal electronic health data and supports their freedom of movement by improving the cross-border exchange of such data to ensure continuity of healthcare. These rights include the right of natural persons or their representatives to access their personal electronic health data through electronic health data access services, the right to insert information in their own electronic health record (EHR), the right to rectification, the right to portability and the right to restrict access to their electronic health data. The rights also contribute to the achievement of the target of 100% of Union citizens having access to their electronic health records by 2030, as set in the Digital Decade policy programme.

For primary use, implementing these rights under the EHDS Regulation requires concrete action, capacity-building and training, to support the digital health community, particularly public authorities, healthcare providers, and service providers, particularly Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs), in the deployment of digital health services and systems that support these rights (across all the priority data categories) and that adopt the EEHRxF (European Electronic Health Record Exchange Format), taking into account the specific circumstances of different categories of stakeholders involved.

For secondary use, the EHDS Regulation requires health data holders, including public authorities and healthcare providers, to create and maintain a dataset description, following a health extension of the DCAT Application Profile [2] (currently under development), and, where applicable, a dedicated labelling for data quality and utility (also under development. These datasets descriptions and labels will need to be made available in the datasets catalogue of health data access bodies (HDABs).

The action is divided in three objectives, each to be achieved through a separate work strand:

a) to build capacity of public authorities, healthcare providers to deploy services and systems that support the rights of natural persons under Chapter II of the European Health Data Space (EHDS) Regulation (primary use);

b) to build capacity of health data holders to improve quality of data, create the datasets description and label for electronic health data they hold and that is within the scope of the EHDS for secondary use;

c) to train service providers, particularly Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs), to support public authorities, healthcare providers and data holders in the implementation of the requirements set by the EHDS.

These objectives will be implemented through three work strands of a single project that will provide cascading funding to the third parties through a single call.

This action will foster a more efficient and interconnected healthcare ecosystem, supporting early adopters including at least public authorities, healthcare providers, health data holders and service providers to advance the implementation of the primary and secondary use requirements in the EHDS.

1 Regulation - EU - 2025/327 - EN - EUR-Lex

2 HealthDCAT-AP Release 5

Scope:

The selected project will manage a portfolio of individual grants across the three work strands by cascading funding mechanism, through financial support to third parties with the maximum amount of up to 120.000 euro per third party. The project consortium will be responsible for selecting, coordinating and monitoring the portfolio of cascaded grants across the three work strands and will ensure their coherent execution in line with the objectives, scope and deliverables defined in the Digital Europe Work Programme 2025-2027 without prejudice to the roles and responsibilities assigned to Health Data Access Bodies under the EHDS Regulation. Therefore, the consortium must demonstrate the ability to develop and execute this type of funding mechanism by involving participants with profound previous experience in this field.

The work of these projects will be implemented through three main work strands:

  1. Work strand 1: The consortium will provide guidance for public authorities and healthcare providers to deploy, upgrade and operate digital health services and systems that support the rights of citizens for primary use of their electronic health data and fulfil their obligations under the EHDS. The consortium will support, through the cascading funding mechanism, activities of public authorities and healthcare providers (e.g. hospitals, clinics, healthcare providers) to deploy digital health services and systems that support the rights of citizens included in the EHDS and the adoption of the EEHRxF, as well as to convert electronic health data into the EEHRxF. As part of the deployment, capacity building activities such as training for staff or reengineering processes can be included.
  2. Work strand 2: The consortium will develop a toolbox to support data holders in preparing electronic health data for secondary use in accordance with the EHDS. Through the cascading funding mechanism, it will support data holders to create and maintain dataset descriptions and, where applicable, data quality and utility labels for electronic health data falling within the scope of the EHDS. This strand will support data holders in publishing dataset descriptions and labels in the dataset catalogues operated by Health Data Access Bodies, thereby enabling data discoverability and access for secondary use. It will also support data holders in putting in place the necessary organisational and technical arrangements to make data available for secondary use under the EHDS, in line with applicable safeguards. Activities under this strand may include, where relevant, supporting data management practices, tooling and workflows, targeted IT deployment, staff training and process reengineering, insofar as these activities facilitate dataset description, cataloguing and secondary use readiness.
  3. Work strand 3: It will develop a training framework and conduct trainings for service providers to prepare them to support public authorities and healthcare providers to deploy digital health services and systems that support the rights of citizens included in the EHDS. It will also prepare them to convert health data held by public authorities and healthcare providers from various formats to the EEHRxF and vice-versa, and to deploy processes and services to enable such conversions, and to create and maintain dataset descriptions and the corresponding labelling for data quality and utility as foreseen in the EHDS for secondary uses of data.

This action is aimed at providing the necessary support, tools, and incentives in complementarity with other associated projects under Digital Europe Programme, EU4Health and Horizon Europe, such as i2X, MyHealth@MyHands, Xt-EHR, TEHDAS2, x-Share, SHAIPED. It should cover a large number of Member States and be deployed supporting all the priority data categories under EHDS. The action contributes to the eHealth Target of the Digital Decade Policy programme established by Decision (EU) 2022/2481 of the European Parliament and of the Council (the ‘DDPP Decision’) [1] through the implementation of EHR systems and digital health services and systems enabling access of citizens to their EHRs as well as contributing to the implementation of the European Data Union Strategy by increasing data discoverability and improved data quality.

1 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dec/2022/2481/oj

descriptionByte:
Risultato atteso:

L'attenzione deve essere rivolta ai settori in cui i paesi del partenariato digitale apportano forti competenze complementari, tra cui imballaggi avanzati, integrazione eterogenea e tecnologie dei chip fotonici. L'argomento mirerebbe a promuovere la collaborazione tra le comunità di R&Amp;I dei paesi del partenariato europeo e digitale. I progetti dovrebbero contribuire ai seguenti risultati:

• Concetti innovativi di progettazione e integrazione per sistemi di calcolo neuromorfico a bassissimo consumo energetico, connettività e funzioni incorporate per applicazioni mobili.

• Tecnologie di processo di fabbricazione alternative per i chip a semiconduttore, compresi il frontend o il backend per l'integrazione eterogenea. Le tecnologie dovrebbero sostenere a medio e lungo termine la rapida evoluzione delle prestazioni, della miniaturizzazione e dei costi dei dispositivi, riducendo nel contempo l'impronta ambientale.

• Soluzioni di imballaggio molto avanzate che mirano all'integrazione eterogenea di molteplici funzioni e materiali per applicazioni in comunicazione (RF, mmW o THz), rilevamento, azionamento, gestione dell'alimentazione e integrazione attiva/passiva.

descriptionByte:
Forventet resultat:

Der skal fokuseres på områder, hvor landene i det digitale partnerskab bidrager med stærk komplementær ekspertise, herunder avanceret emballage, heterogen integration og fotoniske chipteknologier. Emnet vil sigte mod at fremme samarbejdet mellem forsknings- og innovationsfællesskaberne i de europæiske lande og landene i det digitale partnerskab. Projekterne forventes at bidrage til følgende resultater:

• Innovative design- og integrationskoncepter for neuromorfe computersystemer, der understøtter et meget lavt energiforbrug, konnektivitet og indlejrede funktioner til mobilapplikationer.

• Alternative fremstillingsprocesteknologier til halvlederchips, herunder frontend eller backend til heterogen integration. Teknologierne bør på mellemlang og lang sigt understøtte den hurtige udvikling af udstyrets ydeevne, miniaturisering og omkostninger, samtidig med at miljøaftrykket reduceres.

• Meget avancerede emballageløsninger, der sigter mod heterogen integration af flere funktioner og materialer til applikationer inden for kommunikation (RF, mmW eller THz), sensor, aktivering, strømstyring og aktiv/passiv integration.

Onlinemanualen er din vejledning om procedurerne fra indsendelse af forslag til forvaltning af dit tilskud.

Programguiden for Horisont Europa indeholder detaljerede retningslinjer for Horisont Europas struktur, budget og politiske prioriteter.

Ofte stillede spørgsmål om Funding & Tenders Portal – find svar på de oftest stillede spørgsmål om indsendelse af forslag, evaluering og forvaltning af tilskud.

Research Enquiry Service – Stil spørgsmål om alle aspekter af europæisk forskning i almindelighed og EU's rammeprogrammer for forskning i særdeleshed.

Nationale kontaktpunkter – få vejledning, praktiske oplysninger og bistand om deltagelse i Horisont Europa. Der findes også nationale kontaktpunkter i mange ikke-EU-lande og ikke-associerede lande ("tredjelande").

Det europæiske charter for forskere og adfærdskodeksen for deres ansættelse – se de generelle principper og krav, der præciserer forskernes, arbejdsgivernes og finansieringskildernes roller, ansvarsområder og rettigheder.

topicConditions:
Almindelige betingelser

1. Betingelser for antagelse til realitetsbehandling: Forslagssidebegrænsning og layout

Som beskrevet i bilag A og bilag E til Horisont Europa-arbejdsprogrammets generelle bilag.

Begrænsninger for og layout af forslagssider: beskrevet i del B i den ansøgningsformular, der findes i indsendelsessystemet.

Sidegrænsen for del B i ansøgningen om støtte til forskning og innovation (RIA) ved hjælp af et fast beløb er 45 sider. Desuden er det obligatorisk at indsende en detaljeret budgettabel ved hjælp af den skabelon, der findes i indsendelsessystemet.

2. Støtteberettigede lande

Som beskrevet i bilag B til arbejdsprogrammets generelle bilag.

En række ikke-EU-lande/ikke-associerede lande, der ikke automatisk er berettiget til finansiering, har fastsat specifikke bestemmelser om at stille finansiering til rådighed for deres deltagere i Horisont Europa-projekter. Se oplysningerne i programguiden for Horisont Europa.

3. Andre støtteberettigede betingelser

Det Fælles Forskningscenter (JRC) kan deltage som medlem af det konsortium, der er udvalgt til finansiering, som modtager uden finansiering eller som associeret partner. FFC deltager ikke i udarbejdelsen og forelæggelsen af forslaget - se det generelle bilag B.

Som beskrevet i bilag B til arbejdsprogrammets generelle bilag.

4. Finansiel og operationel kapacitet og udelukkelse

Som beskrevet i bilag C til arbejdsprogrammets generelle bilag.

5a. Evaluering og prisuddeling: Tildelingskriterier, pointgivning og tærskler

Som beskrevet i bilag D til arbejdsprogrammets generelle bilag.

5b. Evaluering og prisuddeling: Indgivelses- og evalueringsprocesser

Som beskrevet i bilag F til arbejdsprogrammets generelle bilag og onlinehåndbogen.

5c. Evaluering og prisuddeling: Vejledende tidsplan for evaluering og tilskudsaftale

Som beskrevet i bilag F til arbejdsprogrammets generelle bilag.

6. Retlig og finansiel udformning af tilskuddene

Støtteberettigede omkostninger vil have form af et fast beløb som defineret i afgørelsen af 7. juli 2021 om tilladelse til at anvende faste bidrag under Horisont Europa-programmet — rammeprogrammet for forskning og innovation (2021-2027) — og i aktioner under Det Europæiske Atomenergifællesskabs forsknings- og uddannelsesprogram (2021-2025) [[Denne afgørelse er tilgængelig på finansierings- og udbudsportalen, i afsnittet om referencedokumenter for Horisont Europa under "Afgørelser om forenklede omkostninger" eller via dette link: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/docs/2021-2027/horizon/guidance/ls-decision_he_en.pdf]].

Den tildelende myndighed kan i op til fire år efter foranstaltningens afslutning gøre indsigelse mod overdragelse af ejendomsret eller mod eksklusiv licensudstedelse for resultater, jf. den specifikke bestemmelse i bilag 5.

Som beskrevet i bilag G til arbejdsprogrammets generelle bilag.

Særlige betingelser

Som beskrevet i arbejdsprogrammets specifikke emne.
